title: To-Go
description:
At Texas Roadhouse, we are a people-first company that just happens to serve steaks. Legendary Food and Legendary Service is who we are. We’re about loving what you’re doing today and preparing you for what you’ll be doing tomorrow. Are you ready to be a Roadie?

Pay:

$15.16 per hour

Texas Roadhouse is looking for a To-Go Roadie to support our carry out operations, execute high standards of food quality and service, and ensure our To-Go guests experience the same Legendary Food and Legendary Service as our dine-in guests.

As a To-Go Roadie your responsibilities would include:

  • Ensuring each guest receives a legendary welcome and goodbye when placing and/or picking up their order
  • Uses proper phone etiquette when answering calls and taking orders
  • Knowledgeable of menu to accurately take and place orders
  • Demonstrates strong organization and accuracy when packaging orders
  • Works collaboratively with Back of House staff to complete orders
  • Partners with Restaurant Managers on quote times; accurately provides quotes to guests on the length of time to complete their order
  • Understands our online and mobile app ordering systems
  • Accurately uses point of sale (POS) system to place orders, process To-Go sales, gift card sales, and cash/credit card transactions
  • Practices proper safety and sanitation procedures
  • Exhibits teamwork at all times

If you think you would be a legendary To-Go Roadie, apply today!

At Texas Roadhouse, our Roadies are the heart and soul of our company. We have a fun culture with flexible work schedules, discounts in our restaurants, friendly competitions, recognition, formal training, and career growth opportunities.

Our Roadies are paid weekly. In addition, we offer one of the industry’s most competitive total rewards packages after one year of service to Roadies that meet our benefit eligibility requirements. The total rewards package includes, but is not limited to, the following:

  • A choice of medical plans that are best in class
  • Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 annually
  • Paid vacation time
  • Short-Term Disability
  • Life, Accident, and Critical Illness insurance
  • Identity Theft Protection
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Business Travel Insurance
  • Annual holiday bonus

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, gender, pregnancy, gender identity, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, citizenship, national origin, or any other legally-protected status. We encourage and welcome all applicants to apply.

For more information about this position, please contact the restaurant and ask for a manager.

title: Substance Use Counselor
description:
Overview

Outpatient MAT Opioid Treatment Program

Seeking: Substance Use Counselor - LLMSW. MSW, CAADC or CAADC-DP

Full Time Hours:

  • Monday - Friday: 5:30 AM -2:00 PM

Our Benefits:

  • Semi-Annual Bonus Program
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Competitive 401(k) plan
  • Paid vacation and sick time
  • Employer-paid clinical supervision (free to employees)
  • Free and unlimited access to 500+ accredited Continuing Education Units (CEUs)
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering continued support to employee lifestyle and well-being
  • Early morning hours offering a great work/life balance
  • Opportunity for growth that is second to none in the industry

Our Team:

Western Michigan Comprehensive Treatment Center (CTC), located in Grandville, Michigan is part of Acadia Healthcare's Comprehensive Treatment Centers, the leading provider of medication-assisted treatment in the nation. Our counseling team provides compassionate, high-quality counseling and therapy to patients that are seeking recovery from Opioid Use Disorder.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Provide high quality, compassionate guidance in both individual and group counseling sessions.
  • Plan, oversee, facilitate and document patient's recovery.
  • Co-facilitate assigned group or family sessions as needed.
  • Ensure all documentation regarding patient care, treatment, and incidents is completed timely and in a clear, concise manner.
  • Prepare individual treatment plans for each assigned patient.
  • Initial assessments as well as follow up assessments.
  • Evaluate patient needs and determine if referrals to other programs or facilities are needed.
  • May plan for aftercare for assigned patients.
  • Provide crisis intervention to patients, as needed.
  • Provide case management duties for patients, ensuring individualized quality care as needed.
  • Act as a liaison between referral sources and patients, as needed.

Eligible positions may qualify for student loan forgiveness through HRSA, depending on clinic site eligibility. Check your eligibilty here: HRSA Eligibility

Qualifications

Required Education, Skills and Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in social or health services field required;
  • Degree must be from an accredited college or university.

  • Previous experience in addiction recovery or behavioral health settings, such as outpatient, residential, or correctional facilities.

  • Familiarity with Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT), including methadone, buprenorphine, and naltrexone.

  • Experience conducting individual and group counseling sessions focused on substance use recovery.

  • Knowledge of evidence-based practices, such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Motivational Interviewing (MI), and relapse prevention techniques.

  • Documentation experience, including maintaining clinical notes, treatment plans, and progress updates in accordance with state and federal guidelines.

  • Familiarity with state regulatory standards (e.g., 42 CFR Part 2, HIPAA, Joint Commission standards).

  • Experience collaborating in a multidisciplinary team with medical staff, case managers, and peer support specialists.

Required Licenses/Certifications:

  • MCBAP certification or eligible to apply for a MCBAP Development Plan (applies to CADC/CAAADC)
  • Attained CADC-DP, CADC, CAADC-DP, CAADC
  • Attained LLBSW, LBSW, LLMSW, LMSW, LLMFT, LMFT TLLP, LLP, LP, LLC, or LC

title: Patient Service Specialist
description:
Overview

Are you ready to take your career to new heights? At Concentra, you will be a vital member of our patient care team and play a crucial role in providing exceptional care to our patients. Our mission is to improve the health of America's workforce, one patient at a time. Join us at Concentra and see how your clinical competency and compassion can make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients you serve.

The Patient Service Specialist performs complex administrative duties including but not limited to patient registration, patient scheduling, providing excellent customer service to clients, and management of multi-line phone system. This role requires a general knowledge of various systems and/or procedures. This position ensures that every patient is treated with quality clinical care and is provided a welcoming and respectful experience.

Responsibilities

  • Greet patients and visitors
  • Communicate wait times to patients and direct them accordingly
  • Obtain authorization, as needed, to process patients for services
  • Check in patients using appropriate patient management system
  • Explain all required forms to patients and ensure proper completion of all paperwork
  • Answer incoming telephone lines and direct the caller accordingly
  • Contact patients regarding appointment reminders, rescheduling, or cancellations.
  • Check out patients in appropriate patient management system and distribute records
  • File paperwork, medical records, and correspondence
  • Maintain inventory of office supplies and printed forms
  • Manage dissemination of all paperwork to outside parties including non-injury, custody, and control forms
  • Follow HIPAA guidelines and safety rules
  • Attend center staff meetings
  • Participate in initial and ongoing training as required
  • Complete processing of patient referrals including accurate checkout, paperwork processing, patient education, and communication with Client Support Group
  • Assist Center Operations Director or other leader in managing daily administrative functions
  • Assist in maintaining a neat, clean, and orderly appearance throughout the facility
  • Use employer reporting tool to scan and distribute employer results and paperwork
  • Review clinician transcriptions and enter applicable charges via internal charge entry system.
  • Perform some medical assistant duties such as breath alcohol tests, drug screens, TB skin test reads and/or other duties as assigned/approved by medical leadership

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

Education Level: High School Diploma or GED

Job-Related Experience

  • 6 months to 1 year
  • Working knowledge of state-specific occupational medicine requirements preferred

Job-Related Skills/Competencies

  • Concentra Core Competencies of Service Mentality, Attention to Detail, Sense of Urgency, Initiative and Flexibility
  • Ability to make decisions or solve problems by using logic to identify key facts, explore alternatives, and propose quality solutions
  • Outstanding customer service skills as well as the ability to deal with people in a manner which shows tact and professionalism
  • The ability to properly handle sensitive and confidential information (including HIPAA and PHI) in accordance with federal and state laws and company policies
  • Demonstrated effective communication and interaction with employers, patients, providers, and other employees
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain working relationship with all levels of employees
  • Demonstrated excellent customer service skills
  • Demonstrated intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel, Outlook and entry of data into various systems/applications
  • Ability to perform all aspects of front office operations
  • Drive to achieve or exceed established service standards

Additional Data

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match
  • Medical, Vision, Prescription, Telehealth, & Dental Plans
  • Life & Disability Insurance
  • Paid Time Off & Extended Illness Days Offered
  • Colleague Referral Bonus Program
  • Tuition Reimbursement

title: Senior Infrastructure Specialist zMQ
description:
End Date

Tuesday 15 September 2026

Salary Range

£72,702 - £80,780

Flexible Working Options

Hybrid Working, Job Share

Job Description Summary

Senior Infrastructure Specialist z MQ

Job Description

JOB TITLE: Senior Infrastructure Specialist zMQ

SALARY: £70,929 – £78,810

LOCATION(S): Edinburgh, Manchester or Leeds

HOURS: Full-time – 35 hours per week

WORKING PATTERN: Our work style is hybrid, which involves spending at least two days per week, or 40% of our time, at our Edinburgh, Manchester, or Leeds office.

About this opportunity

This is an exciting time to join our z/OS MQ team. We're at a pivotal point in our transformation, evolving from a traditional infrastructure function into a forward-thinking engineering team focused on automation, simplification, service excellence and innovation. We're looking for passionate, creative individuals with deep MQ expertise who want to help shape the future roadmap for messaging on the mainframe.

In this role, you'll provide highly specialised technical support across critical mainframe environments while contributing to the strategic direction of our MQ platform. You'll help maintain, modernise and evolve our services in line with Group standards, as well as helping drive the adoption of modern engineering practices, DevOps principles and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled capabilities.

You'll help to connect and integrate MQ with a range of modern technologies while ensuring our customers continue to receive resilient, secure and reliable services.

Additionally, you'll provide technical expertise for incident and problem resolution within complex environments, including participation in out-of-hours support and delivery activities when required.

What you’ll do

  • Provide technical leadership and support for complex MQ environments operating to demanding service levels.

  • Help shape the strategic roadmap for z/OS MQ, influencing the future direction of our platform and engineering capabilities.

  • Work closely with key stakeholders and customers to drive and deliver against the technology roadmap, ensuring service and customer outcomes remain at the heart of everything we do.

  • Support the adoption of modern engineering practices, including automation, DevOps and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Collaborate across middleware, infrastructure and engineering teams to explore and implement innovative solutions, integrating mainframe technologies with emerging platforms and capabilities.

  • Promote standardisation, simplification and operational excellence while ensuring processes and controls are adhered to.

Why Lloyds Banking Group

We’re on an exciting journey to transform our Group and the way we’re shaping finance for good. We’re focusing on the future, investing in our technologies, workplaces, and colleagues to make our Group a great place for everyone. Including you!

What you’ll need

  • Extensive knowledge of MQ infrastructure on z/OS.

  • Strong experience of MQ system performance tuning, diagnosis and problem resolution.

  • Experience supporting and troubleshooting business-critical online systems.

  • Experience working with Transport Layer Security (TLS).

  • An interest in driving innovation, automation and the evolution of mainframe technologies.

It would be great if you also had

  • Experience or a keen interest in DevOps practices, automation and modern engineering approaches.

  • An interest in AI and emerging technologies, and how they can be applied to improve engineering effectiveness and customer outcomes.

  • Strong diagnostic skills and the ability to analyse technical information from multiple sources, providing effective solutions in complex environments.

About working for us

Our ambition is to be the leading UK business for diversity, equity and inclusion supporting our customers, colleagues and communities and we’re committed to creating an environment in which everyone can thrive, learn and develop.

We were one of the first major organisations to set goals on diversity in senior roles, create a menopause health package, and a dedicated Working with Cancer Initiative.

We offer reasonable workplace adjustments for colleagues with disabilities, including flexibility in office attendance, location and working patterns. And, as a Disability Confident Leader, we guarantee interviews for a fair and proportionate number of applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the role with a disability, long-term health or neurodivergent condition through the Disability Confident Scheme.

We provide reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process to reduce or remove barriers. Just let us know what you need.

We also offer a wide-ranging benefits package, which includes:

  • A generous pension contribution of up to 15%

  • An annual performance-related bonus

  • Share schemes including free shares

  • Benefits you can adapt to your lifestyle, such as discounted shopping

  • 30 days’ holiday, with bank holidays on top

  • A range of wellbeing initiatives and generous parental leave policies

Want to do amazing work, that’s interesting and makes a difference to millions of people? Join our journey.

At Lloyds Banking Group, we're driven by a clear purpose; to help Britain prosper. Across the Group, our colleagues are focused on making a difference to customers, businesses and communities. With us you'll have a key role to play in shaping the financial services of the future, whilst the scale and reach of our Group means you'll have many opportunities to learn, grow and develop.

We keep your data safe. So, we'll only ever ask you to provide confidential or sensitive information once you have formally been invited along to an interview or accepted a verbal offer to join us which is when we run our background checks. We'll always explain what we need and why, with any request coming from a trusted Lloyds Banking Group person.

We're focused on creating a values-led culture and are committed to building a workforce which reflects the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Together we’re building a truly inclusive workplace where all of our colleagues have the opportunity to make a real difference.

title: Retail Employee
description:
Overview

The Retail Employee / Project Specialist is responsible for performing a range of duties that ensures our customers have an amazing experience whether shopping in our store or picking up an order.

Established in 1978, The Container Store has grown to be the leading specialty retailer of storage and organization products in the United States and the only national retailer solely devoted to the category. We provide creative, multifunctional, customizable storage and organization solutions that help our customers save time, save space and improve the quality of their lives. We foster a culture built around our Foundation Principles, which define how we approach our relationships with our employees, vendors, customers and communities and influence every aspect of our business.

Responsibilities

  • Organizes the stockroom, ensuring it is well-maintained to support selling efforts of the store
  • Adheres to the time expectations established for the role, performing tasks with accuracy and timeliness, while exhibiting pace and attention to detail

We believe in taking care of our team. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package that goes beyond just health insurance (though we've got that covered too!).   • Discounts galore: Enjoy a hefty discount on our amazing products, including merchandise, custom spaces, and services, gift cards, and pet insurance (because fur-babies matter!).

title: Utilities Specialist 1
description:
About this Job

This position plays a key role in supporting the regulation of utility companies and common carriers across Louisiana. Responsibilities include providing technical and analytical support, reviewing applications and tariffs, ensuring regulatory compliance, supporting rate and ownership reviews, investigating consumer complaints, and contributing to hearings when needed.

In this role, you’ll help advance the Commission’s mission to balance fair returns for utilities with safe, reliable, and reasonably priced services for Louisiana customers.

If you’re ready to apply your expertise to impactful regulatory work—from evaluating filings to helping shape decisions that affect utilities statewide—we encourage you to apply today.

Minimum Qualifications

A bachelor's degree in accounting, economics, finance, or statistics.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

  • Review requests for authority from Telecommunications Service Providers (TSP’s). Evaluates the application and proposed tariff for compliance with all LPSC Orders, Rules, and Regulations. Works closely with the Petitioner to resolve any deficiencies, facilitating the application process to completion, including the issuance of a Certificate of Authority.
  • Assists the Legal Division in the review of applications from regulated providers to ensure proper rate application, flow-through procedures, proposed changes of ownership/control, name changes, and assessment of fees in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations, and ensures the utility submits any appropriate required compliance reports timely once a Commission order has been issued.
  • Maintains monthly bill comparisons for water and sewer utilities for distribution to Commissioners and Staff.
  • Maintains record of notices sent from other regulatory agencies detailing any type of enforcement action issued to a utility and tracks the company responses to these enforcement actions and send out notices of these actions to the Commissioners and their Executive Assistants.
  • May testify at LPSC Hearings before an Administrative Law Judge with regard to any Water or Wastewater Utility docketed proceeding.
  • Maintains a working knowledge and is able to interpret Commission Orders concerning the provision of telecommunications services.
  • Evaluates filings from regulated TSPs that make notification of a proposed change of ownership or control, or a proposed change in corporate name, and ensures requests comply with all relevant LPSC Orders, Rules, and Regulations.
  • Reviews applications for authority from Water and/or Wastewater Providers.
  • Receives and investigates complaints regarding rates and services of telecommunications, water, wastewater, electric, or natural gas utilities regulated by the LPSC.

Position-Specific Details:

Appointment Type: Probational and Promotional

Career Progression: This position participates in a Career Progression Group (CPG): Utilities Specialist 1-3. This position provides the opportunity to advance within the job series.

Work Schedule: Work hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday-Friday.

Louisiana is a State As a Model Employer (SAME) that supports the recruitment, hiring, and retention of individuals with disabilities.

How To Apply:

No Civil Service test score is required in order to be considered for this vacancy.

To apply for this vacancy, click on the “Apply” link above and complete an electronic application, which can be used for this vacancy as well as future job opportunities. Applicants are responsible for checking the status of their application to determine where they are in the recruitment process. Further status message information is located under the Information section of the Current Job Opportunities page.

title: Finance Operations Supervisor
description:
Remote Finance Supervisor

Compensation: $80,000k to $90,000k plus 10% bonus

Uniphar – Who we are.

With a workforce of more than 3500 employees spread across Ireland, United Kingdom, Mainland Europe, MENA, and the USA, Uniphar is a trusted global partner to pharma and MedTech manufacturers, working to improve patient access to medicines around the world. Uniphar provides outsourced and specialized services to its clients, leveraging strong relationships with 200+ of the world’s best-known pharmaco-medical manufacturers across multiple geographies, enabled by our cutting-edge digital technology and our highly expert teams. Uniphar is organized into three key divisions: Supply Chain & Retail, Medtech, and Pharma. Click here to find out more: About Us - Who we are | Uniphar

Culture at Uniphar

Uniphar is a combination of many businesses each with their own identity, culture, values, and ways of working. Uniphar lives and breathes four key pillars which unpin and support our culture.

v We have a people first approach - we do the right thing.

v We support an entrepreneurial spirit where adaptability, commitment & resilience is embodied in our way of working.

v We have a Common Purpose that connects our diversified businesses and people.

v Finally, Trust is at the heart of how we operate.

Everything Uniphar does is enabled by our people, and, as we continue to grow domestically and internationally, we become more diverse. This diversity fuels our business and culture.

Sustainability

Sustainability is at the core of what we do and is deeply embedded in our business strategy. We want to contribute positively to the people and the world around us. Running our business in a sustainable way ensures that Uniphar will continue to prosper in the long-term. We are focused on ensuring that each of the five pillars of our sustainability strategy are a fundamental part of our decision-making process.

Role Overview

The Finance Operations Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day finance operations function for Uniphar US, including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, billing, collections, cash application, payroll administration oversight and related transaction controls. The role supervises the Payroll Specialist and AP/AR resources, supports efficient transaction processing through Sage Intacct and ensures finance operations are accurate, timely, scalable and well controlled.

This position is intended to be a hands-on supervisory role rather than a senior manager-level role. The successful candidate will combine practical accounting operations experience with strong process discipline, team coordination and a continuous improvement mindset.

Key Responsibilities

· Finance Operations Supervision

o Oversee daily finance operations across AP, AR, billing, collections, cash application and payroll administration coordination.

o Supervise, guide and support the Payroll Specialist and AP/AR resources, ensuring clear ownership, prioritization and timely completion of recurring tasks.

o Act as the first point of escalation for transactional finance issues, including vendor queries, customer account issues, payroll administration queries and internal process questions.

o Maintain standard operating procedures, checklists and recurring close calendars for core finance operations activities.

· Accounts Payable Oversight

o Monitor vendor invoice processing, coding, approvals and payment preparation in Sage Intacct.

o Review payment runs, vendor statement reconciliations and aged payable items before escalation or approval.

o Work closely with the VP of Finance and Finance Manager to drive process improvements and efficiencies in the AP process.

· Accounts Receivable, Billing and Collections

o Oversee customer invoice preparation, credit note processing, collections follow-up and cash application activity.

o Review AR ageing, unapplied cash, disputed balances and collection priorities.

o Support working capital discipline by identifying slow-paying accounts, recurring billing issues and process bottlenecks.

o Coordinate with commercial, operations and finance stakeholders to resolve customer billing and collection matters.

· Payroll Administration Oversight

o Oversee the payroll administration process performed by the Payroll Specialist, including payroll changes, payroll register review, and deduction updates.

o Coordinate with the company’s PEO/payroll provider for routine payroll processing, employee changes, benefits-related payroll items and payroll reporting support.

o Review payroll outputs and support accurate payroll journal entries, payroll-related reconciliations and Sage Intacct postings.

o Escalate payroll compliance, tax, benefit or employee data issues to Finance, HR and the PEO/payroll provider as appropriate.

· Sage Intacct Process Ownership

o Support effective use of Sage Intacct across transactional finance processes, including coding, dimensions, approval workflows, reporting fields and supporting documentation.

o Identify opportunities to reduce manual work, improve data quality and standardize recurring transaction processing.

o Partner with key stakeholders on practical system improvements, user discipline and process documentation.

· Month-End Close and Controls

o Support month-end close by ensuring timely AP, AR, cash application, payroll and related sub-ledger activity.

o Prepare or review supporting schedules, reconciliations, accrual inputs and transaction reports as assigned.

o Maintain appropriate documentation and evidence of review for finance operations processes.

o Support audit requests and internal control reviews relating to AP, AR, payroll administration and cash activity.

Skills & Experience

· Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or related field preferred.

· 5+ years of accounting operations, AP, AR, payroll administration or shared-services experience preferred.

· Prior supervisory or team lead experience strongly preferred, ideally overseeing transactional finance staff.

· Experience with Sage Intacct or a comparable ERP/accounting system.

· Strong Excel skills and comfort reviewing transactional reports, reconciliations, ageing reports and payroll outputs.

· Practical understanding of AP, AR, cash application, billing, collections, payroll administration and month-end support processes.

· High attention to detail, strong process discipline and ability to manage recurring deadlines across multiple workflows.

· Professional communication style with the ability to coordinate effectively with vendors, customers, employees, Finance, HR and Operations teams.

description:
Job Overview:

Develops and delivers reimbursement and health economics services for Fortrea clients. Serves as an expert strategic consultant and advisor for reimbursement-related projects. Key liaison between customers and healthcare providers and payers as well as governmental bodies in matters of policy. Works independently as well as in collaboration with Business Development to identify and solicit potential clients.     • Market and Sell Services - Contact and call on potential clients to explain the capabilities of the firm with a focus on health economics and reimbursement expertise. Work with Business Development in this capacity. Prepare and review proposals to provide consulting services to clients and execute contracts to provide services and identify opportunities to refer business to other groups or business units within Fortrea Medical Device and Diagnostics.
    • Prepare Proposals with Client Input - Reviews and revise draft health economics and reimbursement proposals/Work Orders that respond to client requirements following standard formats used for previous engagements.

    • Monitor and implement reimbursement policies - Identify and track updates and changes to government policies (Medicare, etc.) as well as policy changes by other healthcare stakeholders including private payers and the AMA that could impact coding, coverage, and payment for medical device companies. Incorporate new policies into reimbursement support initiatives when appropriate.
    • Represent Fortrea to device industry and other organizations - Develop education material for presentations to medical device trade associations, startup incubators, investment groups, etc. via webinars, podcasts, in-person presentations and other means to promote Fortrea’s health economic and reimbursement expertise and capabilities.

Assist in the general marketing of opportunities for the regulatory and clinical groups within Fortrea Medical Device and Diagnostics and serve as a strategic consultant to staff and management as needed.

    • Has a good understanding of the industry, market and our clients and presents Fortrea’s reimbursement and health economics capabilities to clients.

    • Consults with internal SMEs and functional areas as appropriate.

    Leadership:

    • Engages with Fortrea’s leadership to help drive and implement initiatives, including cross business area and functional integrated opportunities, to grow and expand the business.
    • Helps to define and implement the MDD vision and strategy; translates this into key initiatives and priorities; develops and delivers against objectives/plans; able to achieve results in a global, virtual, and complex environment; tracks and measures progress.
    • Partners with peers ensuring consistency (quality, standards, policies, processes, and practices) across the MDD business.
    • Effectively leads in a global, complex environment; sets clear expectations; coaches and mentors for success; consistently communicates and connects; fosters a continuous learning environment.
    • If manager, attracts, selects, on-boards, develops, and retains high performing talent; strengthens and deepens talent bench and succession.
    • Operational Leadership and Financial Acumen:
    • Leads portfolio growth and delivery, encompassing consistent quality.
    • Ensures allocated resources are aligned with current and projected work in terms of capability, quantity, timing, efficiency.
    • Part ownership for the success of the MDD business, including achieving objectives/metrics as assigned. These may include number of new client capability discussions resulting in RFP or proposal, opportunities closed, win %, etc.

    Subject Matter Expertise:

    • Contributes to MDD commercial, operational, reimbursement and scientific leadership and direction, leveraging expertise from other functions as required.
    • Participates in training opportunities to advance knowledge MDD including new areas as MDD leadership sees fit, regulatory changes, GCP, etc.
    • Serves as a senior, strategic consultant to Fortrea clients and Fortrea staff.
    • Provides relevant strategic reimbursement counsel to MDD clients and project teams.
    • Prepares clients, sites, and MDD teams for regulatory inspections; participates in regulatory inspections for clients and MDD projects.
    • Provides leadership as an executive lead and senior principal advisor to clients and MDD teams.
    • Maintains a high level of relevant reimbursement knowledge and shares such knowledge with client and MDD colleagues.
    • Develops and conducts training for clients and Fortrea staff to advance their knowledge of relevant reimbursement requirements.
    • All other duties as needed or assigned.

    Qualifications (Minimum Required):

    • The Senior Principal Advisor typically holds a graduate or post graduate degree in a relevant discipline including but not limited to business administration, public health, public policy, law, clinical science, health services research and health economics.
    • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.

    Experience (Minimum Required):

    • The Senior Principal Advisor has extensive experience developing and executing reimbursement strategies within the medical device industry or as a consultant at Fortrea or in a similar environment and meets the performance criteria outlined by the Firm.

    Preferred Qualifications Include:

    • Related work experience of at least 12 years is preferred.

    Physical Demands/Work Environment:

    • Travel Required 20-30% of the time, with 75% of that time requiring an overnight stay. Travel is primarily within the US.

title: Senior Scientist – Biofermentation & Process Development
description:
Job Title: Senior Scientist – Biofermentation & Process Development

About Us: this is who we are

At Evotec, we believe that curiosity is the spark that drives innovation and success. As a forward-thinking team, we thrive on challenging the status quo, learning from each other, and pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. We're on a mission to create a place where curiosity isn't just encouraged—it’s celebrated.

Are you someone who asks questions, seeks answers, and isn't afraid to go deeper? #BeCureious with us and see where your curiosity can take you!

The Role: / your challenge, …in our journey

We’re looking for a passionate and curious Senior Scientist to join our Reagents team. If you’re excited by new challenges, solving complex problems, and learning every step of the way, you might just be the perfect fit. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to drive impactful projects, collaborate with bright minds, and explore uncharted territories.

As a Senior Scientist at Evotec, you'll have the freedom to ask the hard questions, think outside the box, and find creative solutions that push us forward. It’s a role where your curiosity will fuel both your personal growth and the success of the team.

The successful candidate will join a Protein Science team of ~ 40 members and will be responsible for the expression, particularly fed-batch fermentation using Bioreactors, and purification of a diverse range of protein targets relevant to pharmaceutical research. The ideal candidate will bring deep technical expertise in fermentation science, strong problem‑solving skills, and the ability to work cross‑functionally in a fast‑paced, data‑driven environment.

What You’ll Do:

  • Support project teams by conducting experiments according to defined objectives and timelines.
  • Develop, optimize, and scale up fermentation processes
  • Troubleshoot fermentations performances issues and implement process improvements and corrective measures
  • Independently design experimental routes and implement risk-mitigation strategies; develop optimization and scale-up strategies to achieve project goals.
  • Apply scientific knowledge to troubleshoot and resolve challenges, seeking input from line managers or team members when needed.
  • Prepare written reports, present data, and collaborate with internal and external scientific partners.
  • Present work at project-level and department-level technical meetings as required.
  • Demonstrate full command of all techniques and tools relevant to assigned project responsibilities.
  • Coach and mentor junior colleagues on experimental execution and design.
  • Ensure safe laboratory practices for oneself and any direct reports, adhering fully to company safety policies (including COPs and SOPs).
  • Stay current with scientific literature relevant to assigned projects.
  • Maintain accurate and compliant documentation in accordance with Lab Notebook guidelines.

Who You Are:

  • MS or PhD in Biological Sciences, Biological Engineering, or a related field, with at least 5 years of relevant experience for MS candidates.
  • Strong collaboration skills and ability to effectively partner with the Bioengineering, Expression, and Purification teams at Evotec.
  • A dynamic, accurate, and innovative self-starter with a flexible, problem-solving mindset.
  • Excellent attention to detail and adherence to standard operating procedures, with a commitment to producing high-quality documentation.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in protein expression, including experience expressing diverse protein types in prokaryotic hosts.
  • Experience with Biofermentation process design, development, and optimization for protein production
  • Hands-on experience with fed-batch fermentations using mid-scale BioFlo bioreactors (5 L to 30 L - strongly preferred).
  • Familiarity with high-throughput optimization of expression conditions, including solubility and activity screening, and strategies for increasing protein yield.
  • Experience in protein purification using a wide range of methods and affinity tags
  • Familiarity or proficiency with bioinformatics tools for construct design.
  • Experience working in multidisciplinary teams.
  • The ideal candidate should have demonstrated exceptional client orientation, ensuring clear communication and excellent service delivery.
  • Strong documentation skills, including accurate notebook maintenance and the ability to present results internally and at client meetings.

Why Join Us:

  • Growth Opportunities: We’re a company that believes in continuous learning and development. Whether it’s professional courses, mentorship, or new projects, we’ll help you grow.
  • Flexible Work Environment: We offer flexible work options to help you balance your professional and personal life. This role is site based.
  • Inclusive Culture: We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone’s voice is valued, and curiosity is encouraged.
  • Innovative Projects: You’ll have the chance to work on groundbreaking initiatives and cutting-edge technology in an atmosphere where your curiosity is the key to success.
  • A Place for Big Ideas: We don’t just talk about thinking outside the box—we throw the box away. If you’ve got ideas, we want to hear them.

Are You Still Curious?

If you’ve read this far, then chances are you’ve got a curious mind—just like us. So, what are you waiting for? Take the leap and apply today. We can’t wait to see where your curiosity leads you—and how it will shape the future of Evotec.

Let your curiosity guide your career—#BeCurious and explore the endless possibilities at Evotec!

The base pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be $80,750 to $109,250. Base salary offered may vary depending on the individual’s skills, experience and competitive market value. Job Description:

The Auto Body Technician’s primary responsibility and accountability includes providing an exceptional and successful customer experience through the meticulous assessment and quality repair of each customer’s vehicle to restore it back to pre-accident condition. The Auto Body Technician thoroughly disassembles, repairs, and reassembles each vehicle while playing a pivotal role to our company’s promise of speed, quality and customer excellence. The Auto Body Technician works in alignment with all team members in achieving the repair facilities KPIs and is committed to being a dedicated Brand Ambassador of The Boyd Group at all times.

  • Plans the repair work that is necessary and prepares cost estimates for customers. Uses various tools such as cutting guns, plasma cutters, hydraulic jacks, hammers, and pliers to repair sections of a vehicle.

  • Hammers out dents, dimples, and other minor body damage if possible; mixes and applies filler resins to repair dents when other methods are not feasible.

  • Realigns car chassis and frames to repair structural damage.

  • Removes damaged sections of vehicles and replaces them with new or aftermarket parts. Replaces or repairs glass and windshields as needed.

  • Replaces or repairs interior parts as needed.

  • Welds and otherwise attaches or fits parts into place and Prepares and repaints vehicles with factory-specified paint or agreed-upon equivalent.

Education and/or Experience Required

Required Skills/Abilities

  • Must be able to lift up to 30 pounds at times.

  • Must be able to bend, stretch, kneel, and squat to perform repairs and inspections.

title: Sr. Program Manager - Grid Services
description:
At Sunrun, we’re on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we’re building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. To do it, we’re designing a dynamic culture where employee development, well-being, and safety come first. It’s why we’ve become the #1 home solar and battery company in America. We’re unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle – from sale through installation and beyond – so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with.

Who We Are

We’re on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.


As the nation’s largest residential Clean Tech company, Sunrun is on a mission to transform our energy system into a modern, sustainable grid of the future while making clean, renewable energy accessible to all households.

Sunrun is leading the transition by building Distributed Power Plants (DPPs) and Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) out of home solar and battery assets. Within the Grid Services Revenue Operations & Account Strategy organization, we bridge the gap between technical software capabilities, utility market structures, and profit realization. We are actively hiring world-class talent to operate multi-million-dollar portfolios across open market bring-your-own-device programs, utility bilateral VPPs, competitive energy markets, and next-generation DER offerings (including EV charge management and bidirectional V2X technologies).

As the Northeast Regional Delivery Lead, you will own the operational execution, financial yield, and strategic utility partner relationships across the Northeast footprint—from Maine down through New York, and New England. You will act as the commercial and operational quarterback for a multi-megawatt portfolio, collaborating across Data Science, Product & Engineering, BD, Policy, Marketing, and Customer Excellence. If you thrive on (1) solving complex technical and market optimization challenges, (2) managing multi-million-dollar revenue portfolios, and (3) navigating complex utility integrations, this role is for you.

No candidate will exactly match this job description - please do not hesitate to apply!

NORTHEAST LEAD RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Work within a regional operational team to lead the P&L performance across active open market bring-your-own-device programs including: ConnectedSolutions, CT Energy Storage Solutions, and NY DLC / Pilot Programs.

  • Serve as the primary operational relationship owner and subject matter expert for Northeast utility partners (National Grid, Eversource, O&R, PSEG-LI, etc.), and program administrators.

  • Direct all contractual and regulatory compliance, reporting SLAs, conditions precedent, and monthly/seasonal settlement reconciliations to ensure 100% revenue capture.

  • Ensure technical cohesion with third-party DERMS administrators to streamline program entry and direct integrations.

  • Prepare program operations for next-gen capabilities, including locational delivery, solar sponging, target power commands, and automated dispatch output curves.

  • Collaborate with BD and Policy to showcase performance within existing programs, evaluate regional expansions and new program designs, define operational modeling, customer analytics, and program boundaries.

  • Oversee customer participation journeys, POS T&Cs, and care agents for new customer enrollments, and new product launches.

  • Establish reporting metrics for internal leaders and external reporting requirements and advocacy needs.

TARGET ACHIEVEMENTS

  • Month 1: Familiarize with Sunrun's Northeast Regional Programs, including data architecture, dispatch mechanics, and regional battery control strategies. Take operational ownership of the ConnectedSolutions programs (MA/RI), CT Energy Storage Solutions, and initial NY utility programs.

  • Month 2: Establish working relationships with utility leads (including Eversource, National Grid, Connecticut Green Bank, O&R) and lead recurring roadmap syncs with EnergyHub. Operationalize summer 2027 technical feature builds.

  • Month 3 & Beyond: Assume full P&L oversight for the Northeast regional portfolio. Act as the primary operational SME supporting BD on new contract originations, program launches, and platform productization.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Experience: 5+ years of Program/Project Management experience within energy markets, utility demand response, Virtual Power Plants (VPPs), or Distributed Energy Resources (DERs).

  • Domain Knowledge: Proven understanding of behind-the-meter (BTM) storage assets, DERMS platforms, utility tariff structures, and ISO market mechanics.

  • Technical & Data Skills: Strong analytical capabilities; proficiency in Google Workspace, Salesforce (CRM), and basic SQL/data manipulation preferred. Ability to translate technical data anomalies into actionable business logic.

  • Financial & Commercial Acumen: Comfort managing program P&Ls, contractual obligations, and multi-variable financial risk.

  • Leadership & Communication: Exceptional stakeholder management and presentation skills; comfortable representing Sunrun in front of utility executives, vendors, and regulatory bodies.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Environmental Science, Economics, or equivalent practical experience.

title: Dual Coating & Welding Inspector
description:
About the Organization

E2 Consulting Engineers, LP (E2) is a professional services firm established in 1988 specializing in a full spectrum of engineering services including, project engineering and design, federal base operations and infrastructure support services, gas pipeline construction and inspection services, environmental consulting and remediation, and information technology services. At E2, we value safety, innovation and collaboration, and we are dedicated to excellence.

Overview

E2 Consulting Engineers is seeking a qualified Dual Coating & Welding Inspector to support Client's natural gas pipeline construction projects across Illinois. This specialized dual-certified role combines expertise in both welding inspection and field-applied coating inspection to ensure the highest standards of quality, safety, and compliance on pipeline construction and integrity projects.

The Dual Coating & Welding Inspector plays a critical role in verifying welder qualifications, welding procedures, weld quality, and coating application. This position requires strong technical knowledge of welding codes (API 1104, ASME B31.8) and coating standards, along with the ability to perform comprehensive field inspections across both disciplines.

Responsibilities

Welding Inspection & Quality Assurance

  • Verify that welding procedures are properly qualified and utilized on the project.
  • Confirm that all welders are qualified for the work they are performing and that qualifications are current.
  • Monitor weld quality to ensure sound welds are produced at all joints in accordance with applicable codes and Company specifications.
  • Verify that repairs made to correct weld defects properly address the issue and meet code and specification requirements.
  • Ensure all welding materials are of the proper type and quality, stored correctly, and that damaged materials are not used.
  • Maintain detailed weld mapping, as-built documentation, and proper material traceability (MTRs).

Coating Inspection

  • Inspect field-applied coatings on pipe, fittings, valves, and joints to verify compliance with Company procedures and manufacturer instructions.
  • Perform coating inspections including holiday detection (jeeping), mil thickness verification, and hardness testing.
  • Witness all HDD pull-throughs to verify coating protection and examine the leading edge for coating damage.
  • Complete all required pre-backfill, pre-pull, and post-HDD coating verification checks.

General Pipeline Inspection & Documentation

  • Inspect Other Contractors' work for compliance with permit and one-call requirements.
  • Verify proper material usage, equipment, and safety measures on the jobsite.
  • Complete Daily Inspection Reports, coating inspection forms, safety forms, and other required documentation accurately and thoroughly.
  • Witness hydrostatic testing and verify equipment calibration documentation.
  • Maintain proactive communication with the Chief Inspector regarding daily issues, anticipated problems, and resource needs.

Qualifications

  • AWS Certified Welding Inspector (AWS CWI, SCWI, or CPWI accepted).
  • NACE CIP Level 1 (or current AMPP equivalent).
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of pipeline construction and/or inspection experience (combination of welding and coating experience preferred).
  • Strong knowledge of welding techniques, procedures, consumables, and weld preparation.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, alignment sheets, and valve maps.
  • Familiarity with DOT 192 and OSHA regulations.
  • Knowledge of applicable codes and standards: API 1104, ASME B31.8, NACE, and SSPC.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Word and Excel.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate weld mapping and documentation.

Preferred

  • Experience on urban natural gas transmission pipeline projects.
  • Additional NDT certifications (e.g., MT or PT Level 1).
  • AMPP CIP Level 2 or higher.
  • Experience with horizontal directional drilling (HDD) coating inspection.

Benefits

E2 Consulting Engineers, LP offers an excellent benefits package including health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) with employer match.

Wage Data Per State Requirements

This role will pay $50.00 an hour depending on experience.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

  • Construction Sites and/or Client Right-of-Way (R.O.W.)
  • Client testing facility (occasionally)
  • Corporate office (occasionally)
  • Reports to the Chief Inspector, based locally with respect to the projects.
  • May require extensive driving to reach job sites and/or client/E2 offices.
  • Frequent ascending and descending of ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms up in and out of pipeline bell-hole / trench / excavation.
  • Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling and walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.
  • Lifting objects in excess of 50 pounds from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position
  • Ability to perform visual inspection of construction crew quality of work; using measuring devices; and/or assembly of fabrication parts at distances close to the eyes.
  • Able to perform in both inside and outside environmental conditions in all four seasons throughout the continental United States – extreme cold (temperatures below 32 degrees Fahrenheit) and/or extreme heat (temperatures above 100 degrees Fahrenheit) for periods of more than one hour.
  • May require extensive driving to reach job sites and/or client/E2 offices.

Local Candidates only

No

Drug Free Workplace

E2 Consulting Engineers, LP is a Drug Free Workplace. After accepting an offer of employment, applicants may be required to undergo background checks, drug testing, and/or fit-for-duty physical examination. Drug screens will include, but not be limited to, Amphetamines, Cocaine Metabolites, Marijuana Metabolites (THC), Opiates, and Phencyclidine (PCP). As a federal contractor, E2 cannot permit employees in certain positions to use medical marijuana, even if prescribed by an authorized physician.

Solicitation

Please no solicitation of any kind from agencies, staffing, or recruiting firms.

EEO Statement

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

  • Complete required route/productivity sheets, VCRs and other reports, as required.

For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

  • Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies

title: Counsellor II

_

Counsellor II – Employee Assistance & Total Mental Health Programs

Location: Thunder Bay, ON (Arthur St. Office)

Join Our Team

Be part of our mission to transform how Canadians access mental health support—bringing innovation, compassion, and connection to every client interaction. As a Counsellor II, you’ll provide short-term and longer-term counselling through programs like our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and Total Mental Health (TMH), helping individuals and families in Thunder Bay build resilience.

If you’re a licensed mental health professional who values meaningful client work, teamwork, and flexibility, this is an opportunity to make a real impact within a purpose-driven organization that puts well-being first.

What You’ll Do

As part of our Healthcare Excellence team, you’ll empower clients to navigate life’s challenges and strengthen their emotional well-being through personalized, evidence-based counselling.

  • Deliver Care: Provide solution-focused, goal-oriented brief counselling, alongside opportunities for longer-term therapeutic engagement under TMH and Benefits Extension models.

  • Support the Community: Manage a diverse clinical population presenting with stress, anxiety, relationship issues, workplace concerns, grief, and life transitions.

  • Streamline Workflows: Maintain clear, accurate, and timely clinical documentation using TELUS Health’s integrated digital tools.

  • Collaborate Daily: Participate in interdisciplinary team consultations, peer case reviews, and collaborative groups to ensure seamless continuity of care.

What You Bring

  • Education: Master’s degree in Social Work (MSW), Counselling Psychology, or a related clinical field.

  • Licensure: Current registration in good standing with the OCSWSSW (RSW) or CRPO (RP).

title: Data Analyst
description:

Cronos Europa is a leading IT and digital transformation partner dedicated exclusively to European Institutions and agencies, delivering mission‑critical solutions that shape Europe’s digital future. About the job

We are seeking a Digital Intelligence & Data Analyst to support the analysis of complex digital environments and online information ecosystems. You will transform large volumes of data into actionable insights that support strategic decision-making within one of the European Institutions.

Profile requirements

  • Proven experience in Data Analysis, Digital Intelligence, Business Intelligence, or a related field.

  • Solid understanding of digital media, social networks, and online behavioral trends.
  • Experience in reporting, data visualization, and the generation of strategic insights.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present findings to diverse stakeholders.
  • Ability to work in strategic, sensitive, or institutional environments while handling complex information with discretion.

Desired Assets

While not required, the following qualifications would be considered an advantage:

  • Experience monitoring online influence operations, information risks, or disinformation activities.
  • Knowledge of OSINT, social media analytics, or digital monitoring methodologies.
  • Proficiency with data visualization and business intelligence tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms.
  • Familiarity with data mining, statistical analysis, or large-scale data processing techniques.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams in communications, marketing, public affairs, or strategic advisory environments.
  • Curiosity, critical thinking, and a proactive approach to identifying emerging digital trends and risks.

If you wish to integrate a dynamic structure on a human scale while working with the latest technologies, don't wait anymore and join Cronos Europa!

title: Summer Associate - Water/Wastewater (Summer 2027)
description:
At Clark, we build leaders—individuals who take ownership, rise to challenges, and deliver the Clark standard of excellence. Across the industry, Clark is known for exceptional performance and shaping communities through some of the most complex, high-profile projects being built today.

We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible.

The Role

The Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business. Working as part of the Clark Water team, you’ll be on the front lines of delivering the infrastructure that provides clean water to millions of people—one of our most vital resources.

As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience across project management, field management, project development, and business operations.

Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts.

Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include:

  • The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact.

  • The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge.

This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June.

Responsibilities

Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to:

  • Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.

    • Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions

    • Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process

    • Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installation

  • Field Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.

    • Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safety

    • Project Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics

    • Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordination

  • Project Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasing

    • Budgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bids

    • Estimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects

    • Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractors

  • Business Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization.

Basic Qualifications

  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a graduate degree

  • Interest and passion for the construction industry

What a Successful Candidate Looks Like

We look for individuals who embody these core principles:

1. Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.

2. Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.

3. Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.

A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly.

description:
Come join NRP’s A+ team! We’ve been recognized as a “Top Workplace” because we promote a culture where our team can build long-term careers and connections. As we grow as a company, our goal is that you will grow in your career.

NRP has been recognized with several industry awards including Top Workplaces; Best and Brightest Companies to Work For; and National Apartment Association’s Best Places to Work.

Since its founding in 1994, NRP has been dedicated to building quality homes for our residents, regardless of income. The NRP Group is a full-service multifamily developer, general contractor, and property manager with assets and operations reaching an expanding range of markets nationwide. For additional information, please visit .

Position Summary

The NRP Group is seeking a nationally recognized executive to lead the development of strategic partnerships with Public Housing Authorities (PHAs) and other public-sector stakeholders. This newly created role will establish a proactive national strategy for housing authority relationships, identify new opportunities, and position NRP as a trusted partner in public housing transformation and affordable housing development.

This is a highly relationship-driven, externally focused role—not a traditional development position. The successful candidate will bring significant industry credibility, an extensive national network, and the ability to open doors with housing authority executives, boards, elected officials, and other key decision makers. This executive will identify and cultivate opportunities while partnering with NRP's internal development teams to evaluate and execute them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain senior-level relationships with Public Housing Authority CEOs, Executive Directors, board members, elected officials, and other public-sector leaders.

  • Develop a national strategy for housing authority partnerships and identify priority markets and opportunities.

  • Originate opportunities involving RAD, Section 18, Choice Neighborhoods, LIHTC, mixed-finance, public-private partnerships, and other affordable housing initiatives.

  • Identify partnerships or agreements that may provide strategic benefits to NRP developments, including potential tax exemptions and other public-sector advantages.

  • Leverage an established network to identify opportunities before they are broadly marketed.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and representative of NRP within the public housing and affordable housing communities.

  • Work closely with NRP's local development teams and senior leadership to evaluate and advance opportunities.

  • Represent NRP at national conferences, housing authority events, and industry forums.

  • Help expand NRP's relationships into new markets beyond its existing geographic footprint.

Ideal Candidate

  • The ideal candidate is a seasoned public housing or community development executive with a strong track record of leadership, relationship-building, and an established national network.

  • The candidate may be a current or former:

    • Public Housing Authority CEO or Executive Director

    • Senior housing authority executive

    • Senior leader within a public or community development organization

    • Consultant or advisor to housing authorities or public-sector organizations

  • The successful candidate will have:

    • Deep knowledge of the public housing and affordable housing ecosystem.

    • Strong relationships with housing authority executives, boards, elected officials, and other influential stakeholders.

    • Familiarity with RAD, Section 18, Choice Neighborhoods, LIHTC, and mixed-finance initiatives.

    • Exceptional executive presence, credibility, and relationship-building skills.

    • The ability to quickly establish trust and create access at the highest levels.

    • A strategic, entrepreneurial mindset focused on creating opportunities rather than simply executing transactions.

    • Willingness to travel extensively on a national basis.

Location

This is a national position and does not require the candidate to be based in an existing NRP market. Candidates may be based in any major metropolitan area with strong national relationships.

Success in the Role

Success will be measured by the executive's ability to build a national network of housing authority relationships, create a sustainable pipeline of strategic opportunities, expand NRP's presence in new markets, and establish partnerships that enable NRP's internal teams to successfully execute transformative affordable housing developments.
