title: Real Estate and Facilities Program Manager
description:
Job Description

We have an exciting opportunity for Real Estate and Facilities Program Manager at UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement, based in our Evanston, IL office.

The Real Estate and Facilities Program Manager (maintenance & sustainability) will be responsible for overseeing and managing all aspects of real estate and facilities request process for current UL Research Institutes (ULRI) and UL Standards & Engagement (ULSE) facilities. The Real Estate & Facilities Program Manager (maintenance & sustainability) ensures real estate assets and facilities are optimized to support strategic direction and operational excellence in real estate portfolio management and facility planning.

UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement

At UL Research Institutes (ULRI) and UL Standards & Engagement (ULSE), we expand the boundaries of safety science to create a more secure and sustainable world. For more than a century, we have studied the unintended consequences of innovation, designed solutions to mitigate risk, created new safety standards and shared our findings with academia, scientists, manufacturers, and policymakers across industries. We identify critical safety and sustainability issues, asking the tough questions because we believe a safer world begins with knowledge.

What you’ll learn and achieve:

As the Real Estate and Facilities Program Manager, you will play a key role in the rapid growth of UL as you:

  • Execute the organization’s real estate strategy aligned with its goals and objectives and develop and execute a facilities management program.

  • Ensure all properties and facilities are well-maintained, safe, and compliant with regulations.

  • Oversee space planning, renovation, and construction projects to ensure efficient space utilization and optimal workplace environments.

  • Build-out catalog of support services provided by Real Estate & Facilities Team.

  • Create documentation outlining best practices for site maintenance & sustainability.

  • Track site maintenance & sustainability.

  • Manage vendor relationships, including architects, leasing agents, building space experts, contractors, suppliers, and service providers, to ensure high-quality service delivery and monitor and track facility maintenance activities, including preventive maintenance, repairs, and inspections.

  • Collaborate with the Finance department to develop and manage budgets for real estate and facilities operations, including leasing expenses, capital expenditures, and maintenance costs.

  • Collaborate with the Finance department to conduct financial analysis and forecasting to support decision-making processes related to real estate investments and facility improvements.

  • Implement cost-saving initiatives and strategies to maximize operational efficiency while maintaining high-quality facilities.

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable real estate regulations, building codes, zoning laws, and environmental regulations.

  • Mitigate risks related to real estate and facilities operations by implementing appropriate safety protocols, disaster preparedness plans, and insurance coverage.

  • Stay current on industry best practices, emerging trends, and regulatory changes affecting real estate and facilities management.

  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including executives, department heads, and employees, to understand their real estate and facility needs and align them with organizational objectives.

What you’ll experience working at UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement: We have pursued our mission of working for a safer, more secure, and sustainable world for nearly 130 years, embedding conscientious stewardship into everything we do.

  • People: Our people make us special. You’ll work with a diverse team of experts respected for their independence and transparency and build a network, because our approach is collaborative. We collaborate across disciplines, organizations, and geographies to build the global scientific response that today’s global challenges require.

  • Interesting work: Every day is different for us here. We see what’s on the horizon and use our expertise to build the foundations of a safer future. You’ll have the opportunity to push the boundaries of human understanding as part of a team working to advance the public good.

  • Grow and achieve: We learn, work, and grow together through targeted development, reward, and recognition programs.

  • Values. Four core values guide our work: collaboration, respect, integrity, and beneficence. By living our values, we inspire the trust essential to fulfilling our mission and foster the partnerships that enable us to pursue a beneficent future in which we all can thrive.

  • Total Rewards: All employees at UL Research Institutes are eligible for bonus compensation. We offer comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans and a generous 401k matching structure of up to 5% of eligible pay. Moreover, we invest an additional 4% into your retirement saving fund after your first year of continuous employment. Depending on your role, you may be able to discuss flexible working arrangements with your manager. We also provide employees with paid time off, including vacation, holiday, sick, and volunteer days.

What makes you a great fit:

While no one candidate will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional competencies and personal attributes:

  • Strong knowledge of real estate principles, industry trends, and best practices.

  • Familiarity with building codes, construction, zoning regulations, and environmental standards.

  • Problem solving skills with the ability to identify root causes, develop practical solutions, and work in collaboration with colleagues across the organization to address strategic, operational, and any other roadblocks to success.

  • High degree of curiosity to learn about the mission and impact of the organization and the areas of specialization of its professionals.

  • Excellent financial acumen and budget management skills.

  • Demonstrated expertise in negotiation, contract management, and vendor management abilities.

  • Effective and engaging communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with stakeholders at all levels.

  • Project management expertise to oversee multiple initiatives simultaneously.

  • Attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and ability to make data-driven decisions.

Professional education and experience requirements for the role include:

  • Bachelor’s degree in real estate, construction, facilities management, business administration, or a related field.

  • Minimum 6 years’ experience in real estate portfolio management, facility planning, and facilities management.

  • Experience working with scientific research, academic or research institutions, and experience working with public policy, nonprofit, and/or mission driven organizations are desired.

  • Experience managing facilities with chemical or similar laboratories is preferred.

About UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement

UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement are nonprofit organizations dedicated to advancing safety science research through the discovery and application of scientific knowledge. We conduct rigorous independent research and analyze safety data, convene experts worldwide to address risks, share knowledge through safety education and public outreach initiatives, and develop standards to guide safe commercialization of evolving technologies. We foster communities of safety, from grassroots initiatives for neighborhoods to summits of world leaders. Our organization employs collaborative and scientific approaches with partners and stakeholders to drive innovation and progress toward improving safety, security, and sustainability, ultimately enhancing societal well-being.

To learn more, visit our websites and .

title: Onboarding IAM - Ent Inside Sales Account Manager
description:
Overview

What We Do

We calm the confusion of IT by guiding the connection between people and technology. If a customer is looking for a better way to manage their warehouse inventory, equip their workforce, or secure their data, we make it happen. All it takes is finding the right combination of tech hardware, software, cloud solutions, and support services. That’s what we do. We’re the IT Department’s IT Department.

Who We Are

Our team is made stronger by a multitude of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. It’s what makes Connection unique—what drives us to innovate and create technology solutions that stand apart from the crowd. We’d love for you to be a part of that fabric, to share your ideas and experiences with a team that thrives on fresh thinking, creativity, and helping others.

Why You Should Join Us

You’ll find supportive teammates and a rewarding career at Connection—plus great benefits. We take pride in supporting employees with a total rewards package that provides financial, emotional, and physical resources for you and your family. Our compensation, 401k plans, medical insurance, and other benefits are progressive and competitive. We value the importance of our employees’ emotional wellbeing. To support employees, we provide free therapy visits, mental health coaching and tools, and meditation resources. You’ll also enjoy a generous paid time off package that includes not only vacation and sick time, but also Wellness and Volunteer Time Off days.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Responsibilities

The Onboarding Inside Account Manager (OBIAM) is more than a sales training role—it's the launchpad for a successful career in enterprise technology sales. As an OIAM, you'll combine customer relationship management, consultative selling, and operational excellence while learning from experienced Enterprise Account Executives (EAEs).

In this hybrid role, you'll serve as both an Inside Account Manager (IAM) and Client Experience Specialist, helping new customers experience the best of Connection from day one. You'll partner closely with Enterprise Account Executives, manufacturers, distribution partners, and internal support teams to onboard customers, uncover new business opportunities, drive revenue growth, and deliver exceptional service throughout the customer lifecycle.

If you're motivated by building relationships, solving business challenges, and developing a career in technology sales, this role offers hands-on experience, mentorship, and a clear path for growth.

What You'll Do

Create Exceptional First Impressions

You'll lead a world-class onboarding experience that helps new customers quickly realize the value of partnering with Connection.

  • Deliver a personalized, "white glove" onboarding experience for new enterprise clients.
  • Introduce customers to their dedicated Connection team and available resources.
  • Demonstrate our technology solutions, customer portal, reporting capabilities, and self-service tools.
  • Understand each customer's business priorities, challenges, and strategic initiatives.
  • Configure customer portals, standards, and purchasing workflows to align with business needs.
  • Build trusted relationships with key customer stakeholders from the very beginning.

Develop into a Trusted Sales Advisor

Working alongside experienced Enterprise Account Executives, you'll learn to identify opportunities, support sales initiatives, and contribute to business growth.

  • Support one or more Enterprise Account Executives with proactive sales activities.
  • Develop and manage customer quotes, including technically configured solutions.
  • Maintain a four-hour response goal for customer quote requests.
  • Register opportunities and manage deal registrations with manufacturer partners.
  • Follow up on active proposals and sales opportunities.
  • Identify cross-sell, upsell, and whitespace opportunities within existing accounts.
  • Conduct spend analysis and proactively recommend new technology solutions.

Build Strong Customer Relationships

You'll become a trusted business partner by providing responsive service and strategic account support.

  • Maintain ongoing communication with customers, manufacturers, distributors, and internal teams.
  • Build relationships across multiple customer departments and decision-makers.
  • Help customers maximize the value of their technology investments.
  • Partner with customers on pricing strategies, standards management, and procurement optimization.
  • Deliver Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and proactive account recommendations.

Lead Operational Excellence

You'll coordinate the resources needed to deliver a seamless customer experience from quote through fulfillment.

  • Oversee daily account activity to ensure timely order processing and issue resolution.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Support to maintain order accuracy and meet shipment expectations.
  • Assist with pricing reviews, order escalations, and complex open-order management.
  • Support return merchandise authorization (RMA) escalations.
  • Ensure Salesforce opportunities remain accurate and current.
  • Analyze customer activity and prepare meaningful business reports.

Collaborate and Lead

As your knowledge grows, you'll become a key resource for both customers and teammates.

  • Coordinate activities across Sales, Operations, Customer Support, and manufacturer partners.
  • Mentor and guide Inside Sales Support Representatives on customer priorities.
  • Share best practices and contribute to team success.
  • Support new Enterprise Account Executives during onboarding by introducing company resources, sales processes, and operational tools.
  • Help accelerate new EAE productivity through coaching, collaboration, and ongoing support.

What Success Looks Like

Successful OIAMs:

  • Build lasting customer relationships based on trust and responsiveness.
  • Deliver an outstanding onboarding experience that drives customer confidence.
  • Identify and develop new revenue opportunities within existing accounts.
  • Meet or exceed sales, gross profit, and customer satisfaction goals.
  • Balance multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
  • Collaborate effectively across teams to deliver seamless customer experiences.
  • Continuously grow their sales, technical, and business knowledge.

Why Join Connection?

At Connection, you'll gain exposure to enterprise technology sales while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your success. You'll receive hands-on training, mentorship, and opportunities to build meaningful customer relationships, develop consultative selling skills, and grow into increasingly strategic sales roles.

If you're driven by learning, collaboration, and delivering exceptional customer experiences, this is an opportunity to build a rewarding career with a company that values innovation, partnership, and continuous growth.

This job description outlines the general responsibilities and qualifications for this position. Duties and responsibilities may evolve to meet business needs.

  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities.

title: Customer Journey Expert Commercial Cards / Corporate Card solutions
description:
Customer Journey Expert Commercial Cards / Corporate Card solution

At ING, we aim to improve the digital experience for our customers and help them stay a step ahead in life and business. We also want to make a positive contribution to society and the world we live in. As a Customer Journey Expert, you take ownership of and improve our Commercial Cards offering. Our team empowers clients to pay frictionlessly, stay in control of expenses and grow our Commercial Cards business.

Your department

In Tribe Payments NL, we work to provide customers with the best and most seamless payments journey while growing our portfolio. To realise this ambition, we are looking for a Customer Journey Expert (Product Manager) with knowledge of Commercial Cards and payment products, and experience in developing a commercial cards strategy and roadmap that improves the customer experience.

  • You bring an outside-in view and translate customer needs into a best-in-class strategy and roadmap.
  • You actively define and execute our roadmap and support Sales in positioning our corporate card solutions.
  • Together with the team, you build business cases for new initiatives and portfolio growth and ensure their execution.
  • With stakeholders across domains, including IT, Risk and external parties, you drive change implementation and service integration.
  • You work with external suppliers and partners to drive our product development.
  • You build relevant networks and partnerships inside and outside ING.
  • You work with Risk, Compliance and Legal to ensure our products and services comply with regulations and policies.
  • You bridge IT and business by understanding client needs and digitalization, ensuring high-quality delivery.
  • Together with your colleagues you are responsible for meeting your quarterly goals.

Your team

This position is in the Commercial Cards product team, based in Amsterdam. You will work with 11 Customer Journey Experts on our Corporate Card proposition, customer journeys, risk and IT systems. You will also work closely with engineers in the Netherlands and the Philippines, external suppliers, Sales, Risk, other tribes and payment-chain stakeholders. You will report to the Product Lead Commercial Cards.

Our products serve ING clients from self-employed and micro businesses to corporate clients. Your projects will mainly focus on improving the proposition for Mid-Corporate Banking clients and Corporate Cards clients, many of whom operate internationally. Key challenges include reducing customer friction, growing the business with a distinctive market offering, ensuring regulatory compliance and managing risks.

How to succeed

Our biggest expectation is that you take end-to-end responsibility. As our new Customer Journey Expert, you:

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree and at least five years of experience in payments, PSPs, card issuing or card schemes.
  • Strong knowledge of card payments, preferably Commercial Cards, card issuing and commercial payments.
  • Customer-focused, with the ability to translate client needs into better propositions and services.
  • Commercial mindset and proven ability to deliver results and drive change.
  • Analytical, fact-based and able to make clear decisions.
  • Strong collaborator who can lead projects and challenge constructively.
  • Able to balance regulatory requirements with pragmatic, customer-focused solutions.
  • Energetic, proactive and comfortable working independently and in a team.
  • Fluent in English; Dutch is preferred.

We hire smart people like you for your potential. We expect you to stay curious, keep learning, take responsibility, be a team player and act proactively. In return, we support you in developing into an even stronger version of yourself.

What you can expect from us

  • An agile working environment with innovative colleagues who improve customer solutions every day.
  • A challenging role at the core of ING, with direct impact on Business Banking customers.

Within the Payments Tribe, you can also count on opportunities to invest in your personal and professional growth through the expertise of our teams.

Rewards and benefits
We want to make sure that it’s possible for you to strike the right balance between your career and your private life. Find out more about our employment conditions.


The benefits of working with us at ING include:

  • 25-28 vacation days depending on contract
  • Pension scheme
  • 13th month salary
  • 8% Holiday payment
  • Hybrid working
  • Personal growth and challenging work with endless possibilities
  • An informal working environment with innovative colleagues


About us
Curious about how ING empowers people and businesses to move forward?

Discover what we do and what we can offer you.

Questions?

title: Dean of Academic Success
description:
Apply now to join FAU, where tomorrow begins.


For more information on everything FAU has to offer, please visit .


Note: Current FAU employees must apply as an internal applicant by logging into their existing Workday employee account.

Position Summary:

Florida Atlantic University seeks a strategic, collaborative, and innovative leader to serve as Dean of Academic Success. Reporting to the Senior Associate Vice President for Strategic Planning and Student Success, the Dean serves as a university-wide leader responsible for advancing academic support, advising strategy, enrollment-connected academic planning, and high-impact educational practices. The Dean provides leadership for initiatives that promote student success, defined as student retention, academic progression toward timely degree completion, and readiness for professional or continued educational pathways. The overall goal of the position is to improve undergraduate and graduate student outcomes.


This role provides leadership for cross-functional initiatives that strengthen the connection between enrollment pipelines, academic support structures, educational experiences, and student outcomes. The Dean will drive change, empower faculty and staff, and align institutional efforts with university priorities, Board of Trustees’ direction, and state-level expectations, including those of the Florida Board of Governors.


This role may include leadership or oversight for units and functions such as:

  • Academic support and learning assistance programs
  • University advising services, advising systems, and academic coaching
  • General education oversight and related academic standards
  • Assessment of student success initiatives and progression supports
  • Undergraduate and graduate academic support coordination
  • Undergraduate research, fellowships, honors, and related initiatives, as assigned
  • Additional responsibilities assigned through Academic Affairs or the Provost’s Office

Primary Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership and Institutional Partnership

  • Serve as a senior strategic leader and principal partner to the Senior Associate Vice President for Strategic Planning and Student Success.
  • Lead and advance a university-wide vision for academic success that connects enrollment strategy, academic support, advising, progression, retention, and graduation outcomes.
  • Serve as a thought leader on integrating AI and emerging technology into the curriculum to ensure students build essential career skills.
  • Develop and implement cross-functional initiatives that improve student achievement for undergraduate and graduate students – including through the Enrollment Management Oversight Committee and collaborations with the Graduate College.

Leadership of Academic Success Portfolio

  • Provide direct leadership and administrative oversight for centralized academic success and support functions.
  • Oversee university-wide standards for academic advising, systems, coordination, and student support structures, while partnering with colleges on seamless student-facing experiences.
  • Direct and strengthen the university’s approach to general education oversight, broad curricular policy coordination, and related academic standards.
  • Oversee high-impact practices and collaborate with other units on experiential learning opportunities.
  • Ensure academic support and advising strategies are aligned to the needs of various student populations, including first-year students, transfer students, student-athletes, ROTC students, high-achieving students, and other key populations.

Collaboration with Colleges and Academic Affairs

  • Serve as a bridge-builder across Academic Affairs and related divisions to foster collaboration around institutional student success priorities.
  • Partner with the colleges in ways that support and complement shared governance over discipline-specific curriculum, program content, and major-specific advising.
  • Support broad academic policy development and implementation through university-level committees and governance processes.

Operational and Administrative Leadership

  • Provide leadership for budget, planning, staffing, and organizational development across the academic success portfolio.
  • Support university-level academic processes and designated responsibilities, which may include matters such as academic policy support, academic integrity appeals, grade grievances, or related functions assigned through the Provost’s Office.
  • Advance a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.


Applications will be accepted until the position is filled; however, review of applications will begin September 28, and candidates are encouraged to apply by that date to ensure full consideration. Questions regarding this position may be directed to provost@fau.edu or 561-297-3062, Attn: Geoffrey Johnson, Assistant Vice President for Academic Operations and Initiatives, FAU Office of the Provost.

• A distinguished record of achievement and professional credentials consistent with tenure and a faculty appointment.
• Significant senior-level leadership experience in higher education, preferably in academic affairs, student success, advising, enrollment-connected academic planning, or related areas.
• A commitment to innovation and professional development for high-performing teams.
• Demonstrated ability to build productive partnerships with faculty, deans, executive leaders, and administrative units.
• Experience using data, assessment, and evidence to inform strategy, planning, and decision-making.
• Strong communication, organizational, and change leadership skills.


Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in a large public university or multi-campus environment.
• Knowledge of state university system priorities, accountability frameworks, and governing board expectations.
• Experience overseeing or partnering on general education, broad academic policy, centralized advising systems, or university-level curricular processes.

title: Small Business Credit Analyst
description:
At FNBO, our employees are the heart of our story—and we’re committed to their success! Please see below the details of this career opportunity and how it fits into our organization’s success.

Summary of the Job:

The Small Business Credit Analyst will perform independent credit analysis of small business loan requests (CRE, C&I, and Agribusiness). The analyst also will complete financial analysis and evaluation of credit worthiness. The role will decision business credit applications using sound lending practices and in accordance with all applicable policies, laws and regulations and prepare loan memorandums, risk rating matrices, financial analysis and collateral analysis. The incumbent will develop and maintain a thorough understanding of loan products and procedures and interact with and provide an exceptional customer experience to internal and external customers.

About This Role:

Conduct complete credit underwriting including:

  • Prepare accurate and timely loan presentation packets (credit memos) for new credit requests, loan renewals and annual reviews.
  • Utilize abbreviated underwriting strategies on qualifying requests.
  • Spread and analyze financial information (e.g. CPA prepared statements, tax returns, internal financial statements, etc.) for borrowers, guarantors and related entities.
  • Conduct the appropriate level of guarantor analysis to include: credit bureau reports, personal financial statements and tax returns. Spread and analyze personal guarantor cash flow and provide global cash flow analysis inclusive of all known contingent liabilities.
  • Perform collateral analysis including margin/loan-to-value calculation.
  • Determine the appropriate risk rating for credits using the FNNI risk rating matrix and appropriate verbiage to support the assigned rating.
  • Process requests in a timely manner to ensure desired service levels and compliance requirements are met.
  • Research credit requests including related commitments, background on borrowing entities, analyze industry risks

Approve loan requests within individual designated lending authority.

Become proficient in all operations and procedures of the lending department and related computer systems including the bank’s mainframe system, nCino, and Credit Assessment.

Ensure compliance with loan policy and compliance standards, including the Bank’s BSA/AML program. Complete all assigned compliance training and adhere to internal procedures and controls, as required. Report any known violations of compliance policy, laws, or regulation, as well as suspicious customer and/or account activity.

Provide exceptional customer service to staff, customers, and other related parties in support of the credit process. Work with internal and/or external customers to answer any questions and supply additional support needed to complete underwriting of loan applications.

Exhibit professional behavior and promote positive working relationships. Maintain regular and predictable attendance in alignment with departmental/divisional policy.

Maintain complete and accurate file documentation.

The Ideal Candidate for This Role:

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, or related field or equivalent work experience
  • General understanding of financial statements, lending policies, procedures, practices, and documentation including cash flow and collateral analysis

  • Demonstrate accuracy and thoroughness and monitor own work to ensure quality

  • Proficient in PC operation and demonstrated understanding of Microsoft Office Applications and Outlook

title: Summer Associate (Summer 2027)
description:
At Clark, we build leaders—individuals who take ownership, rise to challenges, and deliver the Clark standard of excellence. Across the industry, Clark is known for exceptional performance and shaping communities through some of the most complex, high-profile projects being built today.

We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible.

The Role

The Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business.

As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience across project management, field management, project development, and business operations.

Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts.

Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include:

  • The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact.

  • The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge.

This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June.

Responsibilities

Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to:

  • Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.

    • Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions

    • Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process

    • Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installation

  • Field Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.

    • Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safety

    • Project Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics

    • Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordination

  • Project Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasing

    • Budgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bids

    • Estimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects

    • Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractors

  • Business Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization.

Basic Qualifications

  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a graduate degree

  • Interest and passion for the construction industry

What a Successful Candidate Looks Like

We look for individuals who embody these core principles:

1. Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.

2. Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.

3. Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.

A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly.

title: X Ray Technician Limited Scope Up To 2500 Bonus
description:
Overview

BONUS UP TO $2,500!

Schedule: Full Time / 40 hours a week / M-F 8a-5p

Location: Lakewood, CO (11185 West 6th Avenue)

Are you ready to take your career to new heights? At Concentra, you will be a vital member of our patient care team and play a crucial role in providing exceptional care to our patients. Our mission is to improve the health of America's workforce, one patient at a time. Join us at Concentra and see how your clinical competency and compassion can make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients you serve.

The X Ray Limited Scope & Medical Support Specialist performs routine x-ray, medical, and testing procedures under direct supervision of the treating clinician as well as supports in other areas of the facility as needed including registration and referral management. This position will also perform routine X-ray examinations in accordance with Concentra policies, practices, and procedures and applicable regulations. This role requires efficient and accurate delivery of one-on-one patient care while thriving in a fast-paced environment. Also will ensure that every patient is treated with quality clinical care and receives an excellent patient experience from welcoming, respectful, and skillful colleagues.

Responsibilities

X-ray Technician Duties

  • Prepare patients for radiologic procedures. Escort patients to dressing and x-ray rooms, provide verbal and/or written instructions and assist patients in positioning body parts to be radiographed. Explain procedures and observe patients to ensure patient care, safety and comfort during the x-ray exam
  • Operate radiologic equipment to produce images of the body for diagnostic purposes. Position radiologic equipment and adjust controls to set exposure time and distance according to specification of examination. Take x-rays following established radiologic requirements and regulations to ensure patient care and safety
  • Use radiation safety measures and protection devices to ensure safety of patients and team members
  • Ensure radiologic equipment remains in working order. Report equipment malfunctions to Center Operations Director
  • Ensure all Radiology workflows are followed and all Radiology reports cross correctly to EMRFollows documentation procedures and completes required documentation related to patient x-ray visit.
  • Maintain all x-ray equipment, including calibration, QA/QC procedures, and record keeping in accordance with current policy and procedures

Medical Support Specialist Duties

  • Perform Department of Transportation (DOT) and Non-DOT drug and alcohol testing
  • Prepare patients for physical examinations, including taking vital signs and any required or requested ancillary testing including but not limited to vaccines and injections, phlebotomy, PFTs, audiogram testing and respirator fit testing
  • Perform rapid screening tests (influenza, strep, mono, glucose, etc.)
  • Assist providers during examination and treatment
  • Responsible for performing routine medical procedures as ordered by treating clinician as well as triaging emergent patients as needed
  • Prepare and assist clinician with procedure set up and injury care
  • Apply bandages, dressings and splints as ordered by the treating clinician
  • Dispense medications and DME as ordered by the treating clinician in accordance with state regulations
  • Complete quality assurance activities on equipment and medical devices as well as testing processes used in the center
  • Maintain supplies, clean rooms and equipment, and stock exam rooms
  • Maintain and operate all medical devices and equipment, including calibration and record keeping in accordance with current policy and procedures
  • Notify supervisor immediately if equipment is not functioning properly, supplies are needed, or facility is not operating as expected
  • In partnership with center leadership, assist with patient flow and volume
  • Keep patients informed of expected wait times during all aspects of the center visit
  • Responsible for clerical tasks in both the front and back office associated with patient care and proper record keeping
  • Ensure accuracy in documentation
  • Perform front office duties: greet patients, obtain authorization, check in/out, communicate wait times, answer multi-line telephone system, and distribute employer results/paperwork as needed
  • Follow HIPAA guidelines and safety rules
  • Attend center staff meetings or huddles as required
  • Assist in maintaining a neat, clean, and orderly appearance throughout the facility
  • Complete any applicable training including but not limited to clinical competency training that occurs monthly.

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

  • High school graduate or GED equivalent
  • Certifications and/or Licenses:
  • Completion of state approved Limited Scope Technician certificate program and license by the state in which employed, if applicable.
  • CPR/First Aid Certification

Job-Related Experience

  • Customarily has at least six months or more of medical assistant experience with knowledge of medical procedures and medical terminology
  • Customarily has at least six months of demonstrated experience in X-Ray and familiarity with routine medical procedures
  • Working knowledge of occupational medicine requirements (state specific) is preferred with prior medical office, healthcare and/or customer service-related experience.

Job-Related Skills/Competencies

The Director, Theranostics and Radiation Science will play a key role in supporting the management, mentorship, and development of the Radiation Sciences team. You will help guide and support team members, fostering collaboration and professional growth within the team.

In addition to leadership, you will oversee key processes and work cross-functionally with divisions across Imaging and Radioconjugate development, including but not limited to Clinical Operations, Preclinical Teams, Pharmacometrics, DMPK, and Regulatory Affairs.   • Optimize and review nuclear medicine imaging protocols, including quality control parameters, image acquisition and reconstruction, radiation dose determination, and protocol dose management.

  • Define requirements and technical support for imaging execution at clinical sites, ensuring proper implementation and adherence to study protocols.

  • Design and oversee quality control protocols, working with both internal teams and external partners for imaging review and processing.

  • Provide training, mentorship, and problem-solving support to internal and external clinical study teams to ensure study objectives are met.

  • Perform image-based, patient-specific dosimetry calculations (internal dosimetry, not external beam radiation therapy [EBRT]).

  • Collaborate with the Radiation Sciences team on imaging protocol optimization, ensuring alignment with best practices in QC, image acquisition, radiation dose management, and compliance with regulatory standards.

  • Support regulatory compliance efforts related to radioactive materials, staying current with guidelines from regulatory and professional organizations (e.g., SNMMI, NRC, and international regulatory bodies).

  • Contribute to research and discovery projects as needed, providing scientific and technical expertise to advance innovation in radiation sciences and molecular imaging.

Basic Qualifications

  • BS degree in physical sciences, mathematics or other physical sciences followed by a graduate degree (M.S. or PhD) in medical physics, physics or related scientific disciplines.

  • Medical physics residency or Post Doctoral training with 5+ years of Industry and/or clinical experience (post residency).

  • Knowledge and Experience with personalized dosimetry for radiopharmaceuticals, experience with programs such as Olinda, MIM and other imaging and dosimetry packages is required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Board certification is preferred but not required.

  • Prior industry experience is preferred but not required.

  • Experience with radiopharmaceuticals, Nuclear Medicine, SPECT and PET imaging techniques, reconstruction, and camera quality control procedures are preferred.

  • Strong concepts in radiation biology and radiation physics are preferred.

  • Advanced technical computer skills and thorough understanding of modern electronic infrastructures relevant to radiological imaging such as DICOM, PACS is required and, client/server architectures and image processing is preferred.

  • Understanding of imaging-related project needs as expressed in a clinical study protocol.

  • Experience with radioactive materials regulations or guidelines from regulatory organizations and professional organizations, (e.g. AAPM, SNMMI, NRC, and other country regulatory bodies)

The Data Management Officer (DMO) is a senior administrative role responsible for advancing enterprise-wide data governance, stewardship, quality, and compliance with Texas Senate Bill 475 (SB 475) requirements. The DMO will serve as a strategic leader in managing institutional data assets, driving data maturity assessment activities, and implementing data management policies aligned with TAMUS data governance frameworks. The position requires deep technical knowledge of data architecture, metadata management, data lifecycle processes, analytics platforms, and best practices in higher education data governance.

The salary is determined in accordance with the University’s compensation structure and will be commensurate with the candidates’ education and experience, within the assigned salary range for this position.

Responsibilities:

Data Governance & Policy

  • Lead development, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise data governance policies, standards, and procedures in alignment with SB 475 and TAMUS expectations.
  • Serve as subject-matter expert for data governance bodies (e.g., Data Governance Council, Data Stewards committees), providing guidance on policy interpretation and data stewardship responsibilities.
  • Coordinate with functional leaders, IT, and institutional research teams to ensure consistent application of data definitions, taxonomies, and standards across academic and administrative domains.

Data Management & Compliance

  • Oversee institutional data inventory development and maintenance, ensuring accurate documentation of data sources, data owners, business rules, and data usage.
  • Drive compliance with SB 475 requirements, including maturity assessment preparation, reporting, and gap remediation planning.
  • Ensure privacy, security, and regulatory compliance related to institutional data, working in collaboration with Information Security, Records Management, and Legal offices.

Data Maturity Assessment

  • Plan, coordinate, and conduct enterprise data maturity assessments using recognized best-practice frameworks (e.g., DCAM, DAMA DMBOK, Gartner, EDM Council).
  • Analyze maturity assessment results and prepare actionable findings, recommendations, and executive briefings to support institutional decision-making and strategic planning.
  • Lead cross-functional teams through assessment activities, data collection, gap analysis, and prioritization of improvement initiatives.

Data Architecture & Technology

  • Provide technical leadership for data integration, data architecture design, metadata management, and master data management (MDM) solutions.
  • Collaborate with IT leadership on data platforms, data warehouses, analytics environments, data quality tools, and APIs to ensure scalable and reliable data infrastructure.
  • Evaluate and recommend tools and technologies that support enterprise data governance, data cataloging, lineage, profiling, and quality monitoring.

Data Quality & Stewardship

  • Establish quantitative data quality metrics, dashboards, and monitoring processes to proactively detect and resolve data quality issues.
  • Empower data stewards across colleges, divisions, and administrative units to own and maintain data quality standards.
  • Facilitate training and awareness programs on best practices in data quality, stewardship roles, and data governance responsibilities.

Reporting & Analytics Support

  • Support institutional reporting initiatives by ensuring underlying data is well defined, governed, and fit for purpose.
  • Collaborate with Institutional Research, Business Intelligence, and Analytics teams to align analytic efforts with governance standards and enterprise data strategy.
  • Provide executive reporting and insights on data governance progress, data maturity status, and emerging risks or opportunities.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in applicable field.
  • Ten years of of progressive experience in data management, data governance, enterprise data architecture, or related roles in large organizations, preferably in higher education.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise data governance initiatives and data maturity assessment efforts.
  • Experience working with senior leaders, data stewards, and cross-functional operational teams to implement data policies and technologies.

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
  • Strong understanding of data governance frameworks (e.g., DAMA DMBOK, DCAM), enterprise data architecture principles, metadata management, master data management, and data lifecycle strategies.
  • Proficiency with data cataloging and data quality tools (e.g., Collibra, Informatica Axon, Alation, Talend, Ataccama).
  • Experience with data warehousing, business intelligence (BI) tools, and analytics platforms (e.g., Oracle/SQL Server, AWS/Azure data services, Tableau, Power BI).
  • Strong understanding of data privacy, security, and compliance standards (e.g., FERPA, HIPAA, GDPR principles, and ITS TAMUS security frameworks).
  • Familiarity with data modeling, data lineage, and data integration methodologies.
  • Excellent leadership, facilitation, collaboration, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports and presentations for executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, programs, and deliverables in a complex, decentralized institutional environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certifications in data management/governance (e.g., CDMP, DGSP, DAMA certifications).
  • Experience with data maturity assessment tools/methods specific to public sector or higher education.
  • Experience within large academic institutions or multi-campus systems.
  • Knowledge of Texas state reporting requirements and compliance landscapes in higher education.
  • Familiarity with Texas SB 475 data compliance requirements.

title: Emergency Room Technician I Part-time 1p-1a
description:
Under general supervision, performs operational tasks related to the admission of inpatients and outpatients coming to the Emergency Department of GBMC. Ability to multitask in fast paced atmosphere while maintaining GBMC values for initial customer service contact. Escort patients as necessary to ED from general waiting room and to radiological areas when necessary. High school or GED. Graduate from an accredited Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), Cardiac Rescue Technician (CRT), or Paramedic program.

Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), Cardiac Rescue Technician (CRT), or Paramedic. Current and valid CPR Certification.

  • Knowledge in medical terminology.

Ability to walk and stand up to ninety percent (90%) of work time and ability to lift and position patients.

  • Normal patient care environment. May have exposure to excessive noise, dust, temperature, and the like.

  • Communicates plan of care related to ED process with patient and family.
  • Assists with cleaning ED rooms.

  • Draws peripheral blood and insertion of Peripheral Intravenous Catheters under direction of RN/MD. Records in EHR.

  • Completes EKG's as necessary and reports results to RN/MD as well as transmission.
  • Follows the basic process for submission/requisition of lab specimens.

  • Assists with transfer of patients or assist with ambulatory patients.

  • Sets up laceration (sterile trays)
  • Performs purposeful rounding using AIDET process.
  • Assists with transporting of patients, under direction/and or supervision of registered nurse, including emergency situations.
  • Stocks patient's rooms and treatment centers with appropriate supplies.
  • Provides family and patient support.
  • Performs post mortempostmortem care as necessary.
  • Performs inventory and completes clothing sheet for all crisis patients and admissions.
  • Cleans, sanitizes, and prepares exam rooms/equipment for next patient.

description:

We're looking for a Manager to lead this team — someone who can translate business data requirements into vendor strategy, negotiate favorable and compliant contracts, and bring product management discipline to how acquired data is enabled, reused, and governed as it moves out (egress) to internal customers. This role sits at the intersection of business needs, vendor management, legal/compliance, and data product strategy — and requires a leader who can operate credibly across all four.

  • Lead and develop a team responsible for discovering, evaluating, and acquiring third-party data sources, including building and maintaining vendor landscapes
  • Partner directly with internal business stakeholders to translate data requirements into sourcing strategy and vendor selection criteria
  • Own end-to-end vendor contracting for data acquisition — partnering with Purchasing and Legal (OGC) on negotiation, statements of work, terms & conditions, and data-specific legal terms to ensure full compliance

  • Establish and maintain Data Sharing Best Practices covering data access, ownership, security, AI/model use restrictions, and regulatory compliance
  • Manage the team's data-portfolio budget in close collaboration with Finance and Leadership

  • Bachelor’s degree required in Business, Data Science, Information Technology, Computer Science, Analytics, Supply Chain, Finance, or a related discipline Master’s degree preferred Experience:
  • 3–5 years of contract negotiation and vendor-management experience, preferably involving third-party data, technology, software, licensing, intellectual property, or professional-services agreements.
  • 3–5 years of demonstrated people leadership experience, including direct team management, coaching, performance development, or leading a team/function.
  • 5+ years of relevant overall experience in data management, procurement, vendor management, product management, business intelligence, technology sourcing, data governance, or a closely related field.
  • Experience in one or more of the following: Purchasing/procurement, data management, product management, or a related technology or business discipline
  • Demonstrated experience negotiating contracts or managing vendor relationships, ideally involving data, technology, or licensing terms
  • Experience partnering with Legal and Purchasing functions on contract terms, statements of work, and compliance requirements

  • Prior people leadership or team management experience

Taylor Corporation is looking for a Press Production Manager to lead daily digital press operations and drive performance across production, quality, safety, employee development, and continuous improvement initiatives. This position is responsible for ensuring customer commitments are met, production schedules are achieved, equipment is operating efficiently, and teams are supported through strong leadership and accountability.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Review production schedules and establish priorities for the shift.
  • Ensure jobs are started, produced, completed, and moved to the next operation on time.
  • Monitor production performance and adjust priorities when equipment or staffing issues affect output.
  • Identify bottlenecks and escalate issues before they impact delivery commitments.
  • Ensure digital presses are operated safely and according to manufacturer specifications.
  • Monitor press performance, run speeds, uptime, downtime, and production output.
  • Coordinate with Maintenance to resolve equipment issues and reduce recurring failures.
  • Establish and maintain quality standards including first-piece approvals and routine quality audits.
  • Lead, coach, and develop press operators while holding employees accountable for performance, attendance, quality, and productivity.
  • Conduct shift meetings and ensure effective communication between shifts.
  • Maintain accurate production information and communicate schedule risks immediately.
  • Monitor key performance indicators including uptime, labor utilization, waste, reprints, first-pass yield, and on-time completion.
  • Enforce safety procedures, PPE requirements, and lockout/tagout practices.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing downtime, waste, changeover time, and rework.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and operator checklists.

You Must Have:

  • Strong understanding of digital presses and production workflows.
  • Experience working in a high-volume production environment.
  • Previous leadership, supervisory, or management experience within a manufacturing setting.

  • Experience leading multi-shift operations.
  • Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related field.
  • Experience within commercial print, direct mail, packaging, or other high-volume manufacturing environments.

title: Sterile Processing Tech, Baptist, PT Weekends
description:
Inspire health. Serve with compassion. Be the difference.

Job Summary

Performs duties in Decontamination, Instrument Preparation and Assembly, and Sterilization/Disinfection relating to cleaning and sterilizing instruments and equipment to be used in patient care. Disassembles complex instruments, supplies and equipment; sorts and inspects for damage and reports needed repairs. Selects the mode of decontamination best suited for items on hand. Assembles, prepares and packages instrument trays, surgical instruments, equipment, and specialty items. Determines the appropriate sterilization or disinfection method and follows appropriate steps for reprocessing. Follows strict documentation guidelines for tray management, biological/chemical test results, equipment functionality, and reprocessing steps.

Essential Functions

  • All team members are expected to be knowledgeable and compliant with Prisma Health's purpose: Inspire health. Serve with compassion. Be the difference

  • Receives, sorts, disassembles and processes contaminated instruments and equipment using the procedures and guidelines as established by Infection Control. Removes soil, blood, tissue fragments and body fluids by wiping, soaking, rinsing, scrubbing and using ultrasonic or other mechanical methods, as applicable.

  • Assembles all instrument sets following prescribed manner and as outlined on the Instrument Count Sheets. Properly documents missing items from the set and labels sets correctly. Takes action to correct problems with instrument sets and reports any unresolved issues.

  • Sterilizes instruments, equipment, linen and supplies using various types of autoclaves and aerators. Reprocesses equipment via high level disinfection as appropriate. Loads and operates machinery in prescribed manner and sets controls to correct specifications for the items being sterilized.

  • Documents all activities related to instrument/equipment decontamination, assembly, disinfection, and sterilization in the Instrument Tracking System (SPM, Censitrac) or established manual systems.

  • Observe and interpret biological, mechanical and chemical monitors relevant to processing/sterilizing. Record results and maintains required records. Initiates recalls as required.

  • Issues items to customers and departments according to established procedures.

  • Observes and reports to supervisor any unfamiliar items with or without appropriate processing literature. Reports equipment requiring repair as needed. Is self-directed and intervenes with corrections to variances in the processing practice.

  • Models Prisma Health behavior expectations. Assists with coaching, mentoring and training coworkers as assigned. Trains and assists with integration of new team members. Shares knowledge, ideas and expertise to support the team and the department.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Supervisory/Management Responsibility

  • This is a non-management job that will report to a supervisor, manager, director, or executive.

Minimum Requirements

  • Education - Completion of job-related coursework: Surgical Tech, Sterile Processing Tech, or Dental Assistant training program.

  • Experience - No experience required.

In Lieu Of

  • In lieu of the education requirement only, will accept High School diploma or equivalent and 6 months experience in a hospital or clinical setting.

Required Certifications, Registrations, Licenses

  • Certification as either: CRCST (Certified Registered Central Service Technician) from HSPA (Healthcare Sterile Processing Association); OR CSPDT (Certified Sterile Processing & Distribution Technician) from CBSPD (Certification Board for Sterile Processing & Distribution) preferred

  • Applicants without sterile processing certification are required to obtain CRCST certification via HSPA within ONE (1) year of meeting the eligibility requirements to sit for the certification exam. Eligibility is defined by HSPA as "10 weeks (400 hours) experience" in a Sterile Processing hospital setting.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • NA

Day (United States of America)

Location

Baptist

Facility

Baptist Hospital

Department

Central Sterile

Share your talent with us! Our vision is simple: to transform healthcare for the benefits of the communities we serve. The transformation of healthcare requires talented individuals in every role here at Prisma Health.

title: Intern – Cybersecurity Risk (Hybrid: Onsite & Remote)
description:
ARE YOU A CURRENT US FOODS EMPLOYEE? PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY THROUGH OUR INTERNAL WORKDAY CAREER SITE

Join Our Community of Food People!

The US Foods Summer Internship Program provides a forum for students to apply classroom skills and academic training in a real-world business environment. In addition to being assigned business-impacting projects throughout the summer, students will be matched with a manager who will meet with them on a regular basis to provide direction on assignments as well as deliver performance feedback and a mentor who will be available to offer day-to-day guidance and support.

Interns will also get exposure to US Foods executive leadership; have an opportunity to participate in learning and social events with other interns across business functions and have an opportunity to deliver an end of summer presentation to showcase their accomplishments with key business leaders.

US Foods internships are full-time paid positions (40 hours per week from June - August) with the possibility of transitioning to a full-time position post-graduation dependent on availability and overall performance.

This position has been segmented as Hybrid meaning the work is a combination of onsite and remote.

Please note: We are unable to provide internships to students that require sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., OPT, F-1, H-1B or any other visa status) now or in the future.

[For Rosemont based internships only] Local candidates are encouraged to apply. For qualified students whose permanent home of record is located outside 50 miles from US Foods Corporate HQ, a sign-on bonus will be offered to partially offset housing costs for the summer.

BASIC PURPOSE:

The Cybersecurity Risk Intern will help support the day-to-day operations of the Technology Governance & Security Team at US Foods. This role will focus on enterprise technology and cyber risk management activities. This role is designed for a student or early-career professional to gain practical experience supporting risk governance processes, risk register administration, remediation tracking and reporting, risk metrics, risk awareness communications, and selected AI and privacy risk management activities. The cybersecurity intern will work with senior members of the cybersecurity team to learn firsthand how enterprise technology and cyber risk management practices are applied in a real-world business environment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Follow and execute directives issued by cybersecurity management and senior employees.
  • Support day-to-day enterprise technology and cyber risk governance activities, including intake tracking, documentation support, workflow monitoring, action item follow-up, and maintenance of records related to risk assessments, risk treatment, and reassessment activities.
  • Assist with maintaining the DigiTech risk register and related repositories by entering, updating, validating, and organizing risk data, ownership details, mitigation status, and supporting evidence under guidance from senior team members.
  • Support the development and maintenance of governance documentation, including procedures, templates, committee materials, SharePoint content, awareness materials, and communication artifacts that help scale enterprise technology risk management practices across DigiTech.
  • Conduct research and basic analysis on technology, cyber, AI, and privacy risks using internal information, stakeholder input, regulatory sources, and industry information to support risk identification, scoring, and governance discussions.
  • Assist with governance activities related to AI and privacy risk management.
  • Learn to manage or utilize tools and solutions implemented for risk management and identification.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

BASIC REQUIREMENTS:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or Master’s Degree in Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, or Information Technology or equivalent degree
  • Must be enrolled in school during time of internship
  • Typically, students currently between their Junior and Senior years or between their 1st and 2nd years of graduate school will be considered for internships
  • Fundamental knowledge of cybersecurity principles and best practices
  • Demonstrative passion for cybersecurity and risk management
  • Basic exposure to cyber security frameworks like NIST CSF preferred
  • Exposure to risk assessments, security assessments and/or governance processes preferred
  • Ability to support activities that measure and track cybersecurity risks, issues, and exceptions
  • Ability to collaborate and work in a team environment

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must have readily available access to high-speed internet
  • Must have regular, reliable method of transportation to commute to US Foods’ location

  • Internal: Core Team, Internal Business Clients

title: Engineer - Water/Wastewater (Winter 2026/Spring 2027 Graduates)
description:
At Clark, we build more than landmark structures - we build leaders. We seek driven individuals who take ownership, rise to complex challenges, and deliver our uncompromised standard of excellence. Known across the industry for exceptional performance, Clark shapes communities through some of today's most high-profile and technically demanding projects. We empower you with real responsibility early in your career, backed by robust resources, structured mentorship, and a culture that pushes you to go further. Here, the standard is higher because we don't just build great projects; we build the people who make them possible.

The Role

The Engineer role is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of our business from day one. Working as part of the Clark Water team, you’ll be on the front lines of delivering the infrastructure that provides clean water to millions of people—one of our most vital resources.

From formal training to mentorship, you’ll develop the technical skills, leadership instincts, and business acumen of seasoned experts. Clark’s network of companies spans every stage of construction, giving you room to explore, specialize, and grow.

Through diverse, hands-on experiences, you will gain invaluable insights across our core operations, including project management, project development, field management, and business operations.

Responsibilities

Your first few years with Clark will be defined by dynamic Career Building Experiences, where you will be exposed to:

  • Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.

    • Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions

    • Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process

    • Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installation

  • Field Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.

    • Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safety

    • Project Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics

    • Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordination ​

  • Project Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasing

    • Budgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bids

    • Estimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects

    • Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractors

  • Business Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization.

As a member of the Clark team, you will be an ambassador for our business and culture. In addition to the core job functions you will learn, you will be expected to:

  • Drive Stakeholder Success: Exceed our clients’ and partners’ expectations by anticipating their needs, desires, and goals.

  • Foster Business Growth: Building meaningful industry connections to bring potential business opportunities to Clark leadership.

  • Recruit the Next Generation of Talent: Embrace our "All team members are recruiters" mindset by building and leveraging relationships to help attract and recruit top talent to Clark.

Basic Qualifications

  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree, with an expected graduation in Winter 2026 or Spring 2027

  • Interest and passion for the construction industry

What a Successful Candidate Looks Like

We look for individuals who embody these core principles:

1. Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.

2. Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.


3. Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.
