title: Safety Coordinator (Winter 2026/Spring 2027 Graduates)
description:
As a Safety Coordinator, you play a vital role in safeguarding the health and well-being of thousands of craft workers and project team members across our jobsites each day. Embedded within general construction operations or one of our specialized affiliate companies, you will work alongside senior leaders to execute safety policies, manage jobsite risk, and actively drive Clark’s "Culture of Care."

Responsibilities

Implementing safe working practices and ensuring the well-being of everyone is a core value of Clark. Safety coordinators are responsible for assisting in the administration of Clark’s Safety, Health, and Environmental program to ensure a safe and healthy environment for Clark employees, trade contractors, and the surrounding community.

  • Enforcing corporate and project-specific safety and health programs as well as federal, state, and local safety standards

  • Promote a positive safety culture through coaching and educating to Clark employees and trade contractors on occupation health and safety requirements

  • Develop and implement project-specific safety program

  • Identify potential hazards and provide immediate input, advice, and direction to mitigate hazardous conditions and assure compliance

  • Conduct site-walks and report project-specific safety performance and future plans

  • Working closely with field supervision to plan complex safety aspects of the project construction, including critical lifts, hazardous material handling, fire prevention, and evacuation

  • Coordinating third-party safety reviews, including OSHA

Basic Qualifications

  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree in occupational health and safety, construction management, engineering, or a related field, with an expected graduation in Winter 2026 or Spring 2027

  • Passion and interest in the construction industry

Preferred Qualifications

  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 trained, preferred

What a Successful Candidate Looks Like

We look for individuals who embody these core principles:

  • Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.

  • Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.

  • Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.

Clark offers a total compensation package that includes base salary, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision benefits, paid time off, retirement/401k, and Company Contribution plan. Additional benefits include life insurance, commuter benefit, short & long term disability, fitness reimbursement, FSA, tuition reimbursement, back-up daycare, tutoring & family support benefits, EAP/Work-Life assistance, and a holiday contribution program. For this role the base salary range is $77,500 - $85,000. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. Base pay is one part of the Total Compensation Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of the Practice and Assistant Director
description:
Job Title

Assistant/Associate Professor of the Practice and Assistant Director

Agency

Prairie View A&M University

Department

Cooperative Extension Programs

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Prairie View, Texas

Job Type

Faculty

Job Description

Important Immigration information:

A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee.

In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.

_______________________________________________________________________________

The Assistant/Associate Professor of the Practice and Assistant Director, under the general supervision of the Professor and Executive Associate Director, is responsible for the day-to-day management, leadership and development of portfolios of outreach with the strategic plan for PVAMU Extension in the College of Agriculture Food and Natural Resources (CAFNR). This position assists in formulating and implementing policy and procedures and provides operational leadership to program teams, conducts independent extension activities related to identified statewide critical issues as outlined in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) plan of work, provides strategic advice on best practices in outreach design and development, outreach management and the agricultural extension landscape.

This position is funded by a grant or restricted funds. Continued employment is contingent on the renewal of grant or restricted funding.

The salary is determined in accordance with the University’s compensation structure and will be commensurate with the candidates’ education and experience, within the assigned salary range for this position.

Responsibilities:

  • Engage faculty/departments, program staff, and stakeholders in constructive dialogues that champion the values of Extension programming and promote regional and statewide needs; leads strategic planning in areas supervised to assess and define the strategic plan of work and measure program impact; advocates for the PVAMU Extension services and seek funding opportunities to sustain and grow programs; plans/initiates and manages cross-functional collaborations to expand land grant mission with CAFNR and Texas A&M AgriLife; participates in statewide planning and promotes the integrated plan of work across mission areas by collaborating with research and academics and other colleges to address relevant community needs; initiates active engagement of department head(s) in annual program briefing and planning meeting in order to assure coordinated approach at state level which includes joint research programming where appropriate; manage annual and long-term personnel planning including recruitment of quality candidates and retention efforts; initiate career ladder trainings for eligible staff; interacts with regional industry leaders, agencies and organizations and solicits input on research and community needs.
  • Supports leadership in advancing continuous improvement efforts to effectively promote the impact of outreach programs across the State of Texas; develops strategies and an operational framework to strengthen community partnerships and collaborative projects; collaborates with colleagues across strategic priority areas to support unit initiatives and ensures accurate project development and reporting within PVAMU Extension systems, including the Program Evaluation and Reporting System (PEARS) and the NIFA Reporting System (NRS); contributes to the design of educational programs aligned with identified needs and strategic priorities; establishes project goals, oversees quality control and assurance, and produces reports and analyses to effectively measure and communicate outcomes and impact.
  • Effectively manages the Extension plan to ensure compliance with established data standards and ethical practices; assists in developing the plan of work and annual budget, while providing operational leadership to agents and specialists to support successful project implementation and strong budget management and forecasting.
  • Evaluates and identifies key community issues relevant to the four program areas; develops, refines, and submits project proposals aligned with the plan of work to address critical regional and statewide priorities; designs, plans, and coordinates priorities that support outreach and educational initiatives; periodically teaches a course that incorporates experiential learning to connect research with academic instruction.
  • Provides leadership and strategic direction to identify and secure funding needed to support the Extension County expansion plan across 100 counties, addressing current and future needs.
  • Monitors compliance with department, University, and/or government standards, policies, and procedures and analyzes existing operations and provides recommendations for improvements; serves on various unit committees and promotes outreach education and productivity by writing proposals, publishing manuscripts, and presenting at professional development conferences.
  • Participates and assists in college-wide events, activities, committees and performs other duties as deemed necessary.

Required Education & Experience:

  • Doctoral degree in Agriculture, Extension Education or related fields.
  • Seven years of experience in Extension programming, applied research, or agricultural administration.
  • Proven leadership, supervisory experience, background in community development, and success in securing grants or funding.
  • Academic, professional, and leadership accomplishments should be commensurate with appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor of the Practice or Associate Professor of the Practice, as applicable.

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Prior work experience with Cooperative Extension, including program development, implementation and evaluation.
  • Effective leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills.
  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.
  • Proven ability to communicate with various audiences, including stakeholders, faculty, staff, and government officials.

title: Associate Director - Medical Science Liaison - Hematology/Oncology (Indiana, Illinois)
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Medical Science Liaison - Hematology/Oncology (Indiana, Illinois)

Company Overview:

At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our 39,000 employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.

Role Overview:

Scientific and Clinical Experts (SEs/CEs) are individuals who are noted for their expertise in a therapeutic area and as a result have special needs for in-depth and cutting-edge information, because they treat patients, design and implement novel research, and educate colleagues and students. The Medical Science Liaison (MSL) program is specifically designed to meet these needs through a field-based group of medical professionals with deep content knowledge about specific disease states, Lilly and competitive compounds and landscape in the therapeutic areas they represent. MSLs recognize and communicate feedback and insights of strategic importance from their interactions with SEs and CEs, to better inform Lilly’s strategic direction for research and commercialization. By facilitating scientific exchange between industry and the scientific community, MSLs have the opportunity to shape the future of healthcare by providing needed information that addresses important clinical and scientific questions.

Responsibilities:

Scientific knowledge

MSLs will be required to engage in continuous learning to maintain the highest level of technical expertise within the therapeutic area they represent. This will enable the MSLs engagement in scientific exchange to respond to the diverse medical information needs based on customer requests. As a result, the MSL will establish themself as a reliable, trusted, resource of unbiased, accurate, up-to-date, medical and scientific information requested by their customers.

Customer engagement

MSLs will spend the majority of their time on customer facing activities. Through the application of emotional intelligence, strategic thinking and a deep understanding of their customers, MSLs will act as one of the primary interfaces between Lilly medical and SEs/CEs to deliver a positive customer experience and utilize MSL capabilities that enhance customer engagement. Additionally, MSLs connect SEs/CEs with other Lilly resources or internal business partners as appropriate and facilitate collaborative research and external opportunities.

Territory ownership

MSLs will be expected to demonstrate strategic analysis, planning, and prioritization to maximize efficiency. They will implement and evaluate a strategic territory plan prioritizing core MSL activities and take personal accountability for results. There is also an expectation for compliant partnerships across all Lilly field roles sharing customers to create an appropriately coordinated experience. MSL will effectively utilize territory analytics for customer identification and routing prioritization.

Strategic vision and leadership

MSLs effectively synthesize and communicate actionable customer/clinical insights to internal Lilly medical and cross functional teams. MSLs use good judgement in decision-making and escalate issues as appropriate. They cultivate internal networks and collaborate effectively across functions including working closely with other field-based colleagues. They embrace change, exercise strategic agility with evolving business needs and utilize innovative resources.

MSLs should always demonstrate the Team Lilly Behaviors in their work with peers and other Lilly colleagues. Within their own team, MSLs are expected to contribute to team goals and be an effective teammate. The MSL will execute the role in a compliant manner, adhering to all governing internal and external requirements, procedures, and laws, always exhibiting good judgement.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in health sciences (e.g., PharmD, MD, PhD in a medically related field) required with 2-3 years of relevant clinical or therapeutic area experience desired.
  • Masters or bachelor’s level degree in health sciences (e.g. BSN, RPh, PA, NP) considered if 5 or more years clinical, research or industry experience in relevant therapeutic area is present.
  • Valid US driver’s license and acceptable driving record are required
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Additional Skills/Preferences:

  • Field based position requires ability to travel up to 80% and work up to 4 to 6 weekends a year.
  • Applicants should live near a transport hub (airport/train station).
  • Intellectual curiosity about the field of science/medicine for which they are responsible.
  • Learning agility to comprehend and effectively communicate large amounts of complex scientific content in a clear and concise fashion.
  • Self-directed and able to work alone in the field effectively managing multiple priorities and projects.
  • Advanced presentation and computer skills with expertise in literature identification.
  • Effective strategic and critical thinking in order to analyze, assess and evaluate information and interpret impact or relevance to future states.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to use field-based electronic or other communication tools for all aspects of job is critical.
  • Resiliency in managing complex challenges.
  • Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills, including high emotional intelligence and the ability to engage in professional relationship building and networking.

Additional Information:

  • Territory covers Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky with primary focus on multiple academic institutions.
  • Employee should be geographically located in or close to Chicago, IL with access transport hub (airport/train station).
  • Experience in servicing customer needs for complex information.
  • Significant experience in professional networking with mutually beneficial outcomes.
  • Experience in field based working environment highly valued.
  • Familiarity with health systems, academic communities, medical research, and medical education process highly valued.
  • Hematology therapeutic area experience is strongly preferred.

title: Team Captain (Shift Leader)
description:
Rally House is where fans celebrate the teams, traditions, and communities they love. Every day is an opportunity to create memorable experiences that bring fans closer to the moments and teams they care about most. The Team Captain helps guide the store team by setting the pace on the floor and keeping the team focused and energized. The Team Captain influences others through example, clear communication, and a strong sense of urgency.

  • Customer Centric: Champions the customer experience by setting the standard for service behaviors. Reinforces expectations, and influences others to consistently put the guest first.​
  • Action Oriented: Acts quickly and decisively to keep work moving forward. Sees opportunities or issues and takes initiative without waiting, maintaining momentum and urgency for the team.​
  • Directs Work: Clarifies priorities and provides direction to others. Ensures alignment, follows up to confirm understanding, and adjusts course when needed to keep the team focused and effective.​

People

  • Support onboarding and training of new team members
  • Help maintain a high-energy, high-commitment store culture
  • Model service behaviors and standards consistently
  • Provide in-the-moment coaching and feedback to team members

Operations

  • Prioritize and delegate tasks during shifts to ensure execution
  • Serve as a go-to resource for basic operational questions
  • Validate completion of daily operational routines
  • Escalate operational risks and gaps to leadership quickly

Merchandising

  • Lead recovery, replenishment, and fixture resets during shifts

  • Guide Teammates on visual standards and product placement

Service

  • Reinforce the Party service model and behaviors

  • Monitor service execution and adjust staffing or focus as needed

Results

  • Drive sales during assigned shifts through guest focus and urgency
  • Coach team members to maximize guest opportunities

Ability to prioritize, delegate, and execute in a fast-paced environment, Clear and confident communication skills, including coaching and feedback, Enthusiastic attitude with a passion for sports and retail, Understanding of retail operations, service standards, and visual merchandising

Qualifications

  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • 1-2 years of retail experience
  • Availability to work 10 to 20 hours per week including daytime, nights, weekends, holidays, and featured local sports events

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to stand and walk for extended periods of time
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds
  • Ability to bend, reach, and climb ladders

$17.00 - $19.50

title: Emergency Room Technician - PRN Days
description:
About Us

HIGHLIGHTS

SHIFT: Day Shift (7am-7pm)

JOB TYPE: PRN

JOB PERKS: Free CEU's!!

We are Emerus, the leader in small-format hospitals. We partner with respected and like-minded health systems who share our mission: To provide the care patients need, in the neighborhoods they live, by teams they trust. Our growing number of amazing partners includes Allegheny Health Network, Ascension, Baptist Health System, Baylor Scott & White Health, ChristianaCare, Dignity Health St. Rose Dominican, The Hospitals of Providence, INTEGRIS Health, MultiCare and WellSpan. Our innovative hospitals are fully accredited and provide highly individualized care. Emerus' commitment to patient care extends far beyond the confines of societal norms. We believe that every individual who walks through our doors deserves compassionate, comprehensive care, regardless of their background, identity, or circumstances. We are committed to fostering a work environment focused on teamwork that celebrates diversity, promotes equity and ensures equal access to information, development and opportunity for all of our Healthcare Pros.

Position Overview

The purpose of this position is to provide technical assistance and supportive patient care to meet the needs of individual patients throughout assigned areas.

Essential Job Functions

  • Collect, report, and document clinical data. Take vital signs, height and weight, intake and output, pulse oximetry, and collect specimens
  • Collect laboratory samples and perform lab testing in accordance with established policies and procedures, as well as COLA and CLIA regulations
  • Assist with patient activities and care as assigned by the charge nurse/designee as indicated by the patient’s plan of care
  • Provide for superficial wound care
  • Provide for patient safety related to age and condition
  • Maintain patient privacy and confidentiality of information and records at all times
  • Provide and maintain a clean, safe environment and perform and/or assist others to perform proper aseptic technique, isolation procedures, and infection control measures

Other Job Functions

  • Prepare patients and chaperone during examinations/procedures or assists with other patient treatments
  • Maintain patient care areas with appropriate supplies
  • Assist with patient restraints and maintain precautions; collect, report and document data related to patient needs/emergencies and unusual patient and family behavior
  • Travel to all facility locations as required
  • Attend staff meetings or other company sponsored or mandated meetings as required
  • Perform additional duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED, required and completion of one of the following:
    • Completion of Medical Corpsman program and one year of applicable experience (or)
    • Completion of EMT-P (Emergency Medical Technician-Paramedic), AEMT (Advanced-EMT), Licensed Paramedic (LP) course/program and one year of applicable experience (or)
    • Completion of the first year of education and current enrollment in an accredited School of Nursing and one year of applicable experience (or)
    • 3+ years of emergency room experience as an ER Technician
  • Current BLS and ACLS certifications, required. PALS preferred
  • Experience with IV start, phlebotomy, and initiation of EKG, preferred

  • Position requires fluency in English; written and oral communication

title: Engineer (Winter 2026/Spring 2027 Graduates)
description:
At Clark, we build more than landmark structures - we build leaders. We seek driven individuals who take ownership, rise to complex challenges, and deliver our uncompromised standard of excellence. Known across the industry for exceptional performance, Clark shapes communities through some of today's most high-profile and technically demanding projects. We empower you with real responsibility early in your career, backed by robust resources, structured mentorship, and a culture that pushes you to go further. Here, the standard is higher because we don't just build great projects; we build the people who make them possible.

The Role

The Engineer role is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of our business from day one.

From formal training to mentorship, you’ll develop the technical skills, leadership instincts, and business acumen of seasoned experts. Clark’s network of companies spans every stage of construction, giving you room to explore, specialize, and grow.

Through diverse, hands-on experiences, you will gain invaluable insights across our core operations, including project management, project development, field management, and business operations.

Responsibilities

Your first few years with Clark will be defined by dynamic Career Building Experiences, where you will be exposed to:

  • Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.

    • Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions

    • Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process

    • Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installation

  • Field Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.

    • Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safety

    • Project Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics

    • Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordination ​

  • Project Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasing

    • Budgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bids

    • Estimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects

    • Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractors

  • Business Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization.

As a member of the Clark team, you will be an ambassador for our business and culture. In addition to the core job functions you will learn, you will be expected to:

  • Drive Stakeholder Success: Exceed our clients’ and partners’ expectations by anticipating their needs, desires, and goals.

  • Foster Business Growth: Building meaningful industry connections to bring potential business opportunities to Clark leadership.

  • Recruit the Next Generation of Talent: Embrace our "All team members are recruiters" mindset by building and leveraging relationships to help attract and recruit top talent to Clark.

Basic Qualifications

  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree, with an expected graduation in Winter 2026 or Spring 2027

  • Interest and passion for the construction industry

What a Successful Candidate Looks Like

We look for individuals who embody these core principles:

1. Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.

2. Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.


3. Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.

Clark offers a total compensation package that includes base salary, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision benefits, paid time off, retirement/401k, and Company Contribution plan. title: Test Automation Engineers
description:
About Our Client

Our client is a multi-award-winning private bank and wealth manager headquartered in the Isle of Man, with offices across London, Jersey, and the UAE. They provide a full international wealth management offering (spanning wealth planning, investment management, and banking services) to both corporate and private clients worldwide.

Job Purpose

We are seeking experienced Test Automation Engineers to join our client's Technology team and play a key role in delivering high-quality solutions across their technology landscape.

Working closely with Software Engineers, Solution Architects, Business Analysts, Product Owners, and key business stakeholders, you will ensure quality is embedded throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC). This role focuses on developing and maintaining automated testing capabilities, elevating quality engineering standards, and supporting the delivery of strategic transformation initiatives.

The position combines technical expertise, quality assurance, automation, and continuous improvement to ensure platforms and services remain reliable, scalable, and fit for purpose.

Responsibilities & Duties

  • Framework Development: Design, develop, and maintain automated test frameworks and test suites across multiple applications and platforms.
  • Quality Assurance: Embed quality engineering principles throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Test Execution: Collaborate with engineering teams to define, create, and execute automated test cases covering functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end testing.
  • Defect Management: Identify, analyze, and troubleshoot defects, working closely with developers to ensure timely resolution.
  • Process Improvement: Support the implementation and continual improvement of testing standards, methodologies, and best practices.
  • DevOps & CI/CD: Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices by integrating automated testing directly into deployment processes.
  • Environment Maintenance: Develop and maintain test data, testing environments, and automation assets.
  • Reporting & Metrics: Monitor test execution results, quality metrics, and coverage to support informed delivery decisions.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Work with BAs, Product Owners, and stakeholders to understand requirements and define effective test strategies.
  • Non-Functional Testing: Support performance, resilience, and reliability testing activities where appropriate.
  • Culture & Mentorship: Promote a culture of quality, continuous improvement, and automation across the Technology function, providing guidance to colleagues on tools and practices.

Skills & Experience

Essential:

  • Proven experience in a Test Automation Engineer, Quality Engineer, or Software Test Engineer role.
  • Direct experience designing, developing, and maintaining automated testing frameworks.
  • Strong knowledge of software testing methodologies, principles, and quality engineering best practices.
  • Hands-on experience with modern automation tools/frameworks (e.g., Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, SpecFlow, or equivalent).
  • Proficiency with API testing tools and methodologies.
  • Experience supporting CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated tests into software delivery processes.
  • Sound understanding of Agile methodologies and SDLC practices.
  • Experience working with cloud-based applications and modern software architectures.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Desirable:

  • Experience working within Microsoft technology environments, including Azure.
  • Broad knowledge of DevOps practices and quality engineering principles.
  • Experience within banking, wealth management, or other regulated financial environments is advantageous but not essential.

title: Automation Engineer
description:
Thank you for your interest in joining Solventum. Solventum is a new healthcare company with a long legacy of solving big challenges that improve lives and help healthcare professionals perform at their best. At Solventum, people are at the heart of every innovation we pursue. Guided by empathy, insight, and clinical intelligence, we collaborate with the best minds in healthcare to address our customers’ toughest challenges. While we continue updating the Solventum Careers Page and applicant materials, some documents may still reflect legacy branding. Please note that all listed roles are Solventum positions, and our Privacy Policy: https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/legal/website-privacy-statement/applicant-privacy/ applies to any personal information you submit. As it was with 3M, at Solventum all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Job Description:

Job Description: Automation Engineer

3M Health Care is now Solventum

At Solventum, we enable better, smarter, safer healthcare to improve lives. As a new company with a long legacy of creating breakthrough solutions for our customers’ toughest challenges, we pioneer game-changing innovations at the intersection of health, material and data science that change patients' lives for the better while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best. Because people, and their wellbeing, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue.

We partner closely with the brightest minds in healthcare to ensure that every solution we create melds the latest technology with compassion and empathy. Because at Solventum, we never stop solving for you.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

As an Automation Engineer – Supply Chain, you will design, build, and maintain RPA bots and intelligent automation workflows that streamline manual, repetitive, and rules-based processes across Supply Chain functions. You will develop scalable, reliable automations using platforms such as UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or Microsoft Power Automate, spanning process discovery, bot design and development, testing, deployment, and ongoing monitoring and support.

In this role, you will build and maintain automation bots and workflows across enterprise systems such as SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft applications, integrate with APIs and enterprise data sources, apply exception handling and orchestration best practices, and implement monitoring, governance, and change-control frameworks to deliver secure, reliable, and production-ready automation solutions.

You will collaborate with Business Analysts, Process Owners, IT Application Teams, Software Engineers, Product Teams, and Supply Chain stakeholders to translate business requirements into scalable automation solutions that reduce manual effort, improve process accuracy, and deliver measurable business impact.

Key Responsibilities

  • RPA & Process Automation Development

Design, build, and optimize RPA bots and automated workflows using platforms such as UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or Power Automate by conducting process discovery and documentation, building reusable components and libraries, integrating with enterprise applications and APIs, and applying coding and design best practices to deliver secure, scalable, and production-ready automation solutions.

  • Automation Testing & Deployment

Design, implement, and manage end-to-end automation testing and deployment pipelines, including unit and regression testing of bots, version control, CI/CD for automation packages, environment promotion (dev/test/production), exception and error handling, scheduling and orchestration, and post-deployment hypercare support.

  • Orchestration, Governance & Monitoring

Manage bot orchestration, scheduling, and queue management using RPA control room/orchestrator tools; maintain a centralized automation pipeline and reusable component library; implement credential and access management, audit logging, and change-control processes; and monitor bot health, run success rates, exceptions, and performance using dashboards and alerting to ensure reliable, secure, and compliant production automation.

  • Collaboration & Engineering Excellence

Collaborate with Business Analysts, Process Owners, IT Application Teams, Software Engineers, Product Teams, and business stakeholders to deliver production-ready automation solutions while driving engineering best practices across process design, bot development, testing, deployment, governance, documentation, and operational excellence.

Skills and Expertise

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field and 4+ years of professional experience in RPA development, business process automation, or software engineering, or a master’s degree with relevant industry experience and 2+ years of experience.
  • Strong proficiency of 4years in at least one RPA platform (UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or Microsoft Power Automate) with hands-on experience building, testing, and deploying production-grade bots and automated workflows.
  • Proficiency in Python, VBScript , Shell script along with SQL, for scripting custom automation logic, data extraction, and integration with enterprise systems and APIs.
  • Experience conducting process discovery and assessment, including process mapping (PDD/SDD documentation), identifying automation candidates, and evaluating feasibility and ROI.
  • Experience implementing automation lifecycle management practices including version control, CI/CD for bots, environment promotion, testing (unit/regression), monitoring, and change management.
  • Experience integrating automations with enterprise applications such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Office/365, and web-based systems, using APIs, screen scraping, and OCR/document understanding tools where needed.
  • Experience using an RPA orchestrator/control room for bot scheduling, queue management, exception handling, and monitoring bot performance, run success rates, and operational reliability.

Additional Qualifications That Could Help You Succeed

  • Experience with intelligent automation technologies such as OCR, document understanding, chatbots, or machine learning models embedded within RPA workflows to handle unstructured or semi-structured data.

title: PRN Histology Technician - Tampa, FL
description:
Overview

We’re hiring a PRN Histology Technician to join our dermatopathology laboratory at Academic Alliance in Dermatology in Tampa, FL. This position provides as-needed support during periods of increased laboratory volume, employee PTO, and unexpected absences. Hours are not guaranteed and will vary based on laboratory needs.

Schedule & PRN Status:

  • This is a PRN (as-needed) position intended to provide coverage during periods of increased laboratory volume, employee PTO, and unexpected absences. Hours will vary based on business needs.
  • Morning availability is required to support embedding, microtomy, and other core histology workflow.
  • Current Florida Clinical Laboratory Personnel license in Histology required.
  • Current HT(ASCP) certification required.

Founded 50+ years ago with a mission to provide the highest quality and full spectrum of medical, surgical, and esthetic skin care services to each and every one of its patients, Anne Arundel Dermatology has assembled the finest group of dermatologists in the Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern states. With 300+ clinicians and 110+ locations in 7 states, we’re thriving, growing, and looking to add talented individuals to our team!

Academic Alliance in Dermatology, an affiliate of Anne Arundel Dermatology, provides comprehensive medical, surgical, and cosmetic dermatology services throughout the Tampa Bay region.

Why join Anne Arundel Dermatology?

At Anne Arundel Dermatology we give exceptional care - to our patients and to each other. We are committed to continual training and education for our physicians and staff. We are on top of the latest developments in dermatology including ongoing research, emerging treatments, new medications and prevention methods. You can find more than just a job with Anne Arundel Dermatology. We believe in providing our new associates with intensive hands-on training and long-term career growth opportunities from within.

Responsibilities

Job Summary: Reporting to the Laboratory Director, the Histotechnician is responsible for specimen processing, tissue preparation, slide production, quality control, and maintenance of laboratory records. The Histotechnician follows established laboratory procedures and ensures the accurate and timely preparation of high-quality histology slides for diagnostic review.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Histology Processing

  • Accurately accession cases into the Laboratory Information System (LIS).
  • Dissect skin and excisional specimens following established grossing protocols.
  • Perform tissue processing and embedding.
  • Perform microtomy and sectioning of paraffin blocks.
  • Perform Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining.
  • Prepare and coverslip slides.
  • Perform quality control and troubleshooting as needed.

Special Stains

  • Operate Special Stain instrumentation.
  • Ensure equipment is functioning properly and producing high-quality slides.
  • Validate staining kits and procedures.
  • Validate and maintain Special Stain controls.
  • Maintain quality control systems for Special Stains.

Immunohistochemistry (IHC)

  • Operate IHC staining instrumentation.
  • Ensure proper equipment function and slide quality.
  • Validate antibodies and staining procedures.
  • Validate and maintain IHC controls.
  • Maintain quality control systems specific to IHC.
  • Assist with inventory management of antibodies and reagents.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain compliance with CLIA, CAP, OSHA, and laboratory policies and procedures.
  • Assist with laboratory quality assurance initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and laboratory records.
  • Communicate effectively with pathologists, physicians, laboratory leadership, and team members.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • HT(ASCP) or HTL(ASCP) certification required
  • Florida License in Histology required
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in a histology laboratory performing:
    • Fixation
    • Specimen processing
    • Embedding
    • Microtomy
    • Reagent preparation
  • Experience with Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry (IHC) preferred
  • Dermatopathology experience preferred

Required Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge and skills consistent with an accredited Histotechnology program
  • If hired into a Mohs laboratory, must meet CLIA requirements for high-complexity testing personnel
  • Knowledge of histology laboratory procedures, equipment, and quality control practices
  • Ability to manage a high volume of work while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail
  • Basic computer proficiency
  • Ability to read and interpret laboratory procedures, manuals, and protocols
  • Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand for extended periods while performing laboratory procedures
  • Frequent use of hands and fingers for laboratory tasks and microtomy
  • Ability to lift up to 40 pounds
  • Ability to work safely around laboratory chemicals and equipment
  • Prolonged periods of sitting and computer work as needed

Licensure/Certifications/Education

PRN employees are generally not eligible for company benefits. To maintain PRN status, employees must work a minimum of two (2) shifts per month.

title: Senior Director, Access Contracting – National Lead
location: Wilmington, Delaware, United States of America
description:
AstraZeneca is seeking a Senior Director, Access Contracting – National Lead to set the strategic direction, performance expectations, and talent agenda for a national team of Community Contracting Account Directors (ACDs).

In this Market Access leadership role, you will guide the execution of AstraZeneca’s biopharmaceutical access programs while partnering closely with Brand, Contracting, Market Access, Sales, and other key stakeholders. Your leadership will help strengthen organizational capability, advance customer partnerships, and ensure the ACD team delivers measurable access impact for customers and the business.

This opportunity is ideal for an experienced leader with strong executive presence, deep Buy & Bill expertise, and a demonstrated ability to build, coach, and lead high-performing teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and develop the national ACD team by setting clear expectations, establishing a culture of accountability, and coaching, mentoring, and developing talent to achieve sustained high performance.

  • Recruit, hire, and retain top talent to build a strong and diverse team with the capabilities needed to meet current and future business objectives.

  • Provide strategic leadership for geographic access plans, including customer prioritization, resource allocation, opportunity identification, and implementation planning aligned with AstraZeneca’s access goals.

  • Apply advanced Buy & Bill business acumen by understanding the economic, operational, and market factors that influence biologics utilization and account decision-making.

  • Maximize field engagement with ACDs and customer accounts to reinforce execution, strengthen team capability, and ensure alignment with customer and business priorities.

  • Drive cross-functional communication and collaboration with Brand Partners, Contracting, Executive and Commercial Business Directors, District Sales Managers, Biologic Sales Specialists, Contract Operations, and other key partners.

  • Lead quarterly business reviews for supported Brand teams, translating access performance, market dynamics, customer insights, and strategic opportunities into concise, compelling, executive-level recommendations.

  • Guide customer and internal business planning, including action plan development, issue resolution, opportunity assessment, and alignment of resources to meet customer needs and AstraZeneca business objectives.

  • Monitor and communicate market intelligence related to competitive activity, healthcare policy developments, reimbursement changes, and other external factors that may affect AstraZeneca’s business or market position.

  • Build and sustain strong customer relationships by identifying solutions, leveraging internal resources, and advancing partnerships that support appropriate access to AstraZeneca’s FDA-approved products.

  • Lead development processes for direct reports, including timely performance appraisals, development planning, coaching conversations, and compensation recommendations.

  • Manage administrative and operational responsibilities with discipline, including budget oversight, expense review, reporting compliance, data accuracy, and coordination with Contract Operations.

  • Represent AstraZeneca externally through participation in industry meetings and conferences, including formal presentations where appropriate.

  • Ensure compliance with the Code of Conduct, the AZ US Policy Handbook, all relevant company policies, and all applicable federal and state laws, rules, and regulations.

About the Team and Role

The Senior Director leads a national team of Community Contracting Account Directors and is accountable for team performance, capability building, talent development, and execution excellence across the organization.

Success in this role requires the ability to lead through influence, develop people at scale, and align a geographically dispersed team around common priorities and measurable business outcomes. The role works across a complex, matrixed environment and serves as a senior partner to functions supporting AstraZeneca’s access programs and business objectives.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Science, Business, or Management.

  • Industry experience: At least 8 years of business experience in the healthcare, pharmaceutical, or biotechnology industry.

  • Buy & Bill experience: At least 3 years of successful Buy & Bill program experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical products industry.

  • Leadership experience: At least 5 years of sales leadership or people management experience.

  • Performance record: Demonstrated record of performance aligned with Brand expectations and business goals.

  • Communication skills: Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with senior internal stakeholders.

  • Talent leadership: Demonstrated success leading, coaching, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Biologics expertise: Experience with biologics across multiple therapeutic areas.

  • Organizational leadership: Strong track record of team leadership, talent development, and organizational performance improvement.

  • Strategic execution: Experience in business planning, market analysis, and strategic execution.

  • Practice-level Buy & Bill programs: Experience implementing biologic Buy & Bill practice-level programs and support at the account level.

  • Matrix leadership: Demonstrated ability to influence across functions and lead effectively in a complex, matrixed environment.

Travel Requirements

Travel is required due to the national scope of the role. Overnight, multi-night, and occasional weekend travel may be necessary to meet business objectives, attend company meetings, and support field engagement.

Join AstraZeneca

If you are an experienced access contracting leader who combines strategic vision, Buy & Bill expertise, and a passion for developing high-performing teams, this is an opportunity to help shape national access strategy and strengthen partnerships across AstraZeneca.

Qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and bring their leadership, customer focus, and commitment to execution excellence to this important role.

title: Supply Chain Clerk
description:
Position Summary

The Supply Chain Clerk is responsible for performing administrative and operational tasks to support supply chain activities. This includes managing inventory records, processing orders, and/or coordinating incoming or outgoing shipments. The role requires attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to follow established procedures to ensure accurate and timely documentation of supply chain activities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Inventory Management:
    • Maintain and update inventory records in the system.
    • Assist with cycle counts and reconcile discrepancies in inventory.
    • Track stock levels and alert supervisors of low inventory.
  • Order Processing:
    • Enter purchase orders, sales orders, and shipping documents into the system.
    • Verify order details for accuracy and completeness.
    • Coordinate with vendors and internal departments to track order status.
  • Shipping & Receiving:
    • Outgoing shipments: prepare shipping labels, packing slips, and bills of lading.
    • Incoming shipments: support receiving activities by logging incoming shipments and verifying quantities against purchase orders.
    • File and maintain records of shipments and receipts.
  • Administrative Support:
    • Maintain supply chain records, including invoices, delivery notes, and purchase orders.
    • Respond to inquiries from internal teams and vendors regarding order status and inventory availability.
    • Assist in preparing reports on supply chain metrics, such as inventory levels and order status.
  • Collaboration & Communication:
    • Exchange information clearly with suppliers, carriers, and internal departments.
    • Provide status updates to stakeholders and clarify requirements when needed.
    • Engage with colleagues to facilitate collaboration and information-sharing.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Education:
    • High school diploma or equivalent required. Associate’s degree or coursework in supply chain, business administration, or a related field is a plus.
  • Experience:
    • 1-2 years of experience in clerical, administrative, or supply chain support roles.
    • Experience with inventory management systems or ERP software is preferred.
  • Skills:

    • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.


Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. title: Sr. Product Manager, NVC Buy
description:
We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.


Enterprise Technology plays a critical part in shaping the future of mobility. If you’re looking for the chance to leverage advanced technology to redefine the transportation landscape, enhance the customer experience and improve people’s lives, this is the opportunity for you. Join us and challenge your IT expertise and analytical skills to help create vehicles that are as smart as you are.

In this position...

Ford Motor Company is looking for a Senior Product Manager, for Non-Vehicle Commerce, to own and evolve the end-to-end cart, checkout, and confirmation experiences on Ford.com and Lincoln.com. This is a high-visibility role at the heart of Ford's digital commerce strategy — you will be accountable for turning intent into completed transactions, ensuring every customer can move seamlessly from "add to cart" to "order confirmed," whether they choose to buy fully online or reserve online and pick up at the dealer.

You will lead a small but critical team (including a direct-report Product Manager focused on Pricing & Promotions), partner closely with the mobile app team to build a truly omnichannel commerce experience and serve as a hands-on mentor and thought leader who raises the bar for Product Management across the broader Product organization.

Although this is classified as a remote position, candidates who are in commuting distance to a Ford hub location may be required to be onsite four or more days per week.

What you'll do...

Own the Buy Experience End-to-End

  • Define and drive the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for cart, checkout, and order confirmation across Ford.com and Lincoln.com for non-vehicle products.
  • Design seamless, low-friction purchase paths that support multiple customer journeys — fully online purchase, online-to-dealer pickup, and hybrid transactions.
  • Continuously identify and eliminate friction points in the funnel, using data, customer research, and testing to improve conversion, completion rates, and overall satisfaction.

Lead & Develop Talent

  • Directly manage and mentor the Product Manager responsible for Pricing & Promotions, ensuring pricing display, discounts, incentives, and promotional logic are seamlessly integrated into the checkout experience.
  • Set clear goals, provide regular coaching and feedback, and support the career growth of your direct report.
  • Act as a role model and informal mentor to other Product Managers across the organization, sharing product best practices, frameworks, and lessons learned.

Drive Omnichannel Innovation

  • Partner closely with the mobile app product team to ensure a consistent, connected buying experience across web and app.
  • Champion an omnichannel mindset — ensuring cart state, pricing, promotions, and order status persist seamlessly as customers move between devices, channels, and touchpoints (online, app, and dealer).
  • Bring an external, customer-first point of view to the team, identifying opportunities to bring best-in-class retail commerce patterns into the automotive buying journey.

Be a Product Leader

  • Bring deep product management expertise — strong discovery habits, rigorous prioritization, and a bias for iterative, data-informed delivery — and use it to inspire and elevate other Product Managers.
  • Set the standard for how to leverage AI to assist with product requirements, experiments, and success metrics that are defined and communicated within the Non-Vehicle Commerce team.
  • Actively contribute to shaping product processes, rituals, and culture that drive innovation across the broader digital product team.

Partner Cross-Functionally

  • Collaborate with engineering, UX/design, analytics, dealer operations, legal/compliance, and marketing to deliver high-quality releases.
  • Work with dealer-facing and operations teams to ensure the "buy online, pick up at dealer" experience is smooth and consistent for both customers and dealers.
  • Define and track key performance indicators and report progress to stakeholders and leadership.

You'll have...

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience

  • 6+ years of product management experience, with a track record of owning commerce, checkout, or transactional experiences at scale.

  • 3+ years of experience managing or mentoring other product managers, or clear readiness to take on people leadership.
  • 3+ years of experience and understanding of e-commerce funnels — cart, checkout, payments, pricing/promotions, and order confirmation flows.
  • 3+ years of experience building or supporting omnichannel experiences that bridge web, mobile app, and physical/in-person (retail or dealership) touchpoints.


Even better, you may have...

  • MBA or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Design or related field

  • Experience with pricing and promotions engines or systems.

  • Familiarity with dealer/retail network operations, particularly "buy online, pick up in store/dealer" models.
  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable using data, A/B testing, and customer research to make and defend product decisions.
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners and senior stakeholders.
  • Passion for customer experience and a demonstrated ability to simplify complex transactional journeys
  • Retail or automotive retail experience
  • Experience working in agile/scaled agile product organizations.
  • Background in automotive, big-ticket retail, or other considered-purchase e-commerce categories.

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:

  • Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
  • Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up childcare and more
  • Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
  • Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
  • Tuition assistance
  • Established and active employee resource groups
  • Paid time off for individual and team community service
  • A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day
  • Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time.

This position is leadership level 6 and ranges from $132,800- 250,800.

Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.

description:
Overview

Discover endless opportunities to grow and make your mark at Hines.

Responsibilities

The Hines Early Experienced Rotation Program is designed to offer a hands-on learning experience, the ability to gain exposure to multiple disciplines within the firm, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Throughout the program, rotational employees will have the opportunity to interface with senior leaders, be mentored by industry experts, and work closely with seasoned professionals. The Rotation Program is a two-year program, spending 1 year in each area within development and investment management.

  • Full-time hires will start as a cohort in June of 2027.
  • Rotation locations may include Chicago, Houston, New York City, DC Metro, Atlanta, Los Angeles or San Francisco.
  • Placement in each location is determined by business demand, and one can look forward to changing geographic locations at least once during the two-year program.
  • Throughout both rotations, you’ll be an integral part of your team and have a wide variety of hands-on experiences. You’ll develop a thorough understanding of the fundamentals of relationship management, underwriting and portfolio management.
  • You’ll receive ongoing mentorship and career development from seasoned leaders, helping you build the necessary skills, competencies and experiences to accelerate your career. Challenging team and individual projects, client interaction, broad business exposure, along with an immersion into multiple areas of the business.
  • Upon program completion, you’ll be given the opportunity to explore roles within Hines across all business areas and geographies.

Within Investment Management, rotations might include:

    • Fund management, portfolio management/modeling, debt financing, investor relations, capital markets, Digital Strategy, ESG, SPO.
  • Underwriting of potential fund investments, create financial models as part of investment underwriting process, creation of investment materials
  • Contact & meet with other real estate professionals including investors, developers, landlords and other brokers.

Within Development:

  • Participate in the management of existing projects.
  • Financial analysis, acquisition opportunities, feasibility analysis, entitlement processes, market research and construction management.
  • Participation in design meetings, interfacing with sellers and capital partners, & investor requirements.

  • Demonstrable interest in commercial real estate.
  • Computer proficiency and experience with financial modeling in Excel.
  • Familiarity with Argus a plus.
  • Work indoors approximately 99% of the time and outdoors 1% of the time.
  • Operate personal computer and other office equipment.
  • Ability to lift up to 25lbs.

At Hines, we strive for excellence as a leading global real estate investment manager, driven by our by our belief that real estate is fundamentally about people. Our diverse portfolio spans $93.2 billion¹ of assets across such property types as living, office, retail, mixed-use, logistics and life science projects – all designed to enhance value, connection and inspiration. Our strategic approach integrates local expertise with global knowledge, taking calculated risks aligned with our convictions to exceed expectations and tailor solutions to our clients' needs.

While our projects are renowned for enhancing cities and pioneering sustainable practices, we recognize that the true driving force behind Hines' success is our 5,000 dedicated employees in 30 countries who draw on our 65-year history to build the world forward. This is why we prioritize investing in our people, offering comprehensive training, competitive compensation, robust benefits and generous vacation packages. By centering our focus on the growth and wellbeing of our team, we cultivate an inclusive environment where everyone, including our clients, can thrive.

Hines is proud to be named to Fast Company’s prestigious annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2024. ¹Includes both the global Hines organization and RIA AUM as of December 31, 2023.

We are an equal opportunity employer and support workforce diversity.
